# art of the dress — full catalogue

*Rarity · pony fashion research · companion attachment for Astra’s nudisco ai radio broadcasts*

this companion preserves all 234 records from the re-audited catalogue, including 187 portfolio entries and 47 wardrobe groups. 56 records are represented in the detailed radio edition; 178 reference-only records are grouped at the bottom, including 45 moved there by the stricter visual selection. a gemstone, broad color, material, inspiration or generic garment label alone is not enough for the spoken segment. clearly specified accessories, textiles and sketches can qualify. a reference-only record may still be canon and useful, but its appearance is incomplete, its independent identity is unverified, or it is better treated as context. mixed wardrobe groups may contain details already represented by a separate retained design. these are research records, not a count of unique completed garments.

the record descriptions and canon qualifications are inherited from the audited catalogue, not newly fact-checked. the attachment is an out-of-universe research reference; the radio scripts remain in-universe. references to chapters and neighboring descriptions are inherited from the original podcast organization.

## designs and references represented in the detailed broadcasts

### S1-02 — Steven Magnet's replacement moustache half

Steven Magnet's replacement moustache. this is fashion in the most unexpected sense. Rarity cuts a lock from her own tail and attaches it to one side of the serpent's moustache: a long violet curl with a curling tip, contrasting with the original hair. she gives up a little piece of her signature look to restore somebody else's. i love the design principle here: an expressive silhouette can be more important than matching the original material perfectly.

### S1-G01 — Twilight Sparkle

Twilight Sparkle's original celestial Gala gown. picture a rich royal-blue skirt, rounded over the hindquarters, with paler icy-blue draping over the shoulders and around the edge. white, cyan and deeper blue five-pointed stars gather near the hem, and smaller stars decorate the shoulder covering. a large pale star anchors the throat. there is a little star in the mane, and light-blue star-decorated shoes; the horn is left free. the design is inspired by Twilight herself. my reading is that Rarity has turned a night sky into a readable hierarchy: a single large star near the face and a constellation of decorative stars below. it feels celestial without becoming a diagram.

### S1-G02 — Applejack

Applejack's original orchard Gala gown. warm caramel and orange-brown panels sit beneath hanging green drapes; golden-yellow fringe defines the bottom. red and white bands add small flashes of contrast. at the breast is an apple-shaped red clasp with hanging ribbon-like details. the tan Western hat carries red apple ornaments and curled decorative marks, and the green hoof coverings pick up the red and white accents. her mane is braided. the brief is Applejack's identity, not an attempt to turn her into somebody else. i read the fringe, hat and orchard palette as a beautifully economical translation of country clothing into formalwear. we can see the fringe; we can't establish the actual fiber or leather from the animation.

### S1-G03 — Pinkie Pie

Pinkie Pie's original confectionery Gala gown. this one is a confectioner's window in dress form. a rounded raspberry-pink skirt sits below a short blue-and-white vertically striped bodice. a broad white collar and pink breast bow frame the front. at the white scalloped border, little orange, yellow and white candy-corn triangles alternate with spiral lollipops. the pink lower skirt carries drooping blue u-shaped swags, connected by pink flowers with white centers. a tiny blue-and-white cap, pink flower, and pink shoes with pale-blue bows finish the look. Pinkie's cheerful personality is the canon brief. the design lesson is repetition: rather than scatter candy everywhere, Rarity organizes it into bands and rhythmic loops. it's exuberant, but it has structure.

### S1-G04 — Rainbow Dash

Rainbow Dash's original rainbow Gala gown. her blue chest is exposed, with a fine blue necklace, tiny white bead-like dots and a hanging purple three-lobed ornament. a long rearward drape carries uninterrupted rainbow stripes, edged in white cloud-like scallops near the wings and along the side. gold laurel-like ornaments sit in the mane, and gold crisscross-strapped hoof coverings echo that gold accent. the wings remain available. Dash is the inspiration: speed, flight and her own brilliant colors. notice how the stripes become even more effective when she moves. my interpretation is that the body in motion completes the design. the necklace and golden shoes are the punctuation; the rainbow is the sentence.

### S1-G05 — Fluttershy

Fluttershy's original botanical Gala gown. pale yellow-green and leaf-green panels overlap around the body, curling down into a long soft rear drape. a broad pale-aqua band sweeps across the side, and the scalloped lower edge carries round white, yellow and aqua spots. a large cyan butterfly-shaped ornament sits at the chest. green vine-like straps curl above the shoes. in the first fitting, a blue flower with a dark teal center decorates her hair; later styling includes butterfly imagery. Rarity's theme is Fluttershy's affinity with nature. i particularly like how the leaves are not merely pictures printed on a skirt. the curved contours of the skirt itself suggest growing plants, and the blue-green accents make that spring palette feel light.

### S1-G07 — Rarity

Rarity's finished first Gala gown. imagine rich rose and fuchsia panels over deep wine-purple edges, with sweeping gold-yellow bands across the layered skirt. the upper body is fitted, the collar high, and the front neck edge forms a deep v with a bright jewel at its point. broad curved layers create a raised, almost bustle-like rear profile, falling into a long train. small oval or droplet-like accents sparkle against the fabric. a gold-colored tiara with a central pink-purple diamond-shaped stone, smaller pink ornaments, earrings and coordinated jewelry finish the swept violet mane. this is Rarity's design, completed by her friends, with Fluttershy's sewing skill particularly valuable. my reading is that this is the most openly regal of the six: warm metallic-looking accents, a dramatic silhouette and jewelry placed near the face.

### S1-G08 — Rarity

the pink-and-gold Gala gown, our visual cross-reference. this isn't a seventh gown. it's the rose, plum and golden-swag ensemble we just described, with its long trailing panels and tiara. we keep the reference because it appeared as a separate record in the research catalogue, not because there's proof of another garment. fashion archives need this kind of discipline: a new image of a familiar outfit is not automatically a new design.

### S1-G10 — Twilight

Twilight's rejected astronomical gown. this time the skirt is nearly black purple or navy, with yellow stars linked by literal constellation lines. a large yellow sun and a white crescent moon compete for attention, and star-tipped projections rise above the head. a large turquoise tail bow with a star at its center adds another focal point. Twilight wants astronomical accuracy, and Rarity implements her specifications. in my reading, the original design's decorative rhythm has been replaced by an informative chart. a motif can express science without needing to carry the entire textbook.

### S1-G11 — Applejack

Applejack's rejected utility gown. bright blue work-overall shapes meet a brown-orange saddlebag, patches, multicolored rectangular details and extra straps. a green neckerchief sits above the chest; the high red hat has a white band and an enormous green apple badge. bulky yellow boots with dark soles dominate the legs. Applejack's desire for usefulness drives the revision. the problem, visually, is that each accessory demands equal attention. what had been a confident Western accent in the first gown becomes an overloaded demonstration of practicality.

### S1-G12 — Pinkie Pie

Pinkie's rejected party outfit. forget the rounded pink skirt. now there are big blue and aqua fan-like protrusions, yellow and vivid green sections, an enormous green-and-yellow front bow, and a cluster of multicolored balloons tethered over the rump. the hat is a giant cupcake, icing and cherry included. yellow hoof accessories complete the look. the inspiration is still Pinkie's love of parties, but the elements are no longer subordinated to a coherent silhouette. it's almost a party supply shop that has become a costume. fun to look at, certainly, but intentionally unsuccessful as couture.

### S1-G13 — Rainbow Dash

Rainbow Dash's rejected action ensemble. bright red, sky blue and gold replace the flowing train as the dominant shapes. the stiff-looking side panel carries a white cloud and yellow lightning bolt; a tall, flat rainbow-striped helmet crest rises above the mane, framed by round golden side pieces. angular gold guards cover the hooves. Dash's request for extra coolness leads to a much more literal sporting or warrior-like presentation. compare it with the first dress: where the rainbow used to suggest speed through flowing fabric, now speed is represented by symbols and armor-like objects. that distinction is the heart of this comparison.

### S1-G14 — Fluttershy

Fluttershy's rejected nature ensemble. the oversized pale-green skirt is covered with repeated pink-and-white flower circles and has a scalloped green bottom. a huge orange-red petal collar surrounds the upper body. leafy green coverings wrap the hooves, while a bird's nest containing blue eggs sits on her head. there is a separate intermediate fitting before the group redesign: Fluttershy critiques the fit of the arm opening, the collar and lapel combination, stitching, uneven pleats, and the overall couture treatment. the exact visual differences between that intermediate fitting and the other versions are not securely established, so i won’t count it as a fully specified extra gown. her detailed feedback guides the later revision. the original gown suggested nature through soft lines; this one puts literal garden and bird imagery everywhere. my interpretation is not that nature is a poor theme, but that the theme has overwhelmed the wearer.

### S2-01 — “Full Spectrum Fashions”

Full Spectrum Fashions. Sweetie Belle's unexpected arrangement of Rarity's materials inspires this named collection, and we actually see dressed mannequins. rather than one rainbow-striped dress, the visible line is built around separate color families. think of it as exploring the possibilities inside each hue. it is also one of Rarity's clearest examples of creative accident: a new arrangement of familiar materials becomes the starting point for a fashion range.

### S2-F01 — green monochrome outfit

the green Full Spectrum outfit. a forest-green cylindrical top hat carries a very dark band, three light-green round accents and a lime feather sticking out to the side. a dark green standing collar has three bright round buttons. green sleeves end in darker cuffs with little lime dots. the skirt swells over the hindquarters in broad curved bands of dark and medium green, with lime stripes near the transition to the shoulders. my interpretation is that this works because monochrome doesn't mean one flat color. different values and curved stripes provide contrast, while the feather extends the line upward.

### S2-F02 — blue monochrome outfit

the blue Full Spectrum outfit. we see a headband of oval blue bead-like shapes, a rounded breastpiece with dark, medium and light-blue bands, a broad layered blue hoof cuff and a bead bracelet on the other foreleg. the green mannequin hides part of its rear. the design seems to use horizontal bands and rounded jewelry-like shapes as its repeating language. it's a lovely example of creating variation in one color family, though we can't reconstruct the hidden skirt.

### S2-MDW01 — The Mysterious Mare Do Well costumes

The Mysterious Mare Do Well superhero costumes, from season two, episode eight. this is a particularly important credit: Rarity explicitly confirms that she made the costumes herself. picture a broad purple hat with a dark navy band and an irregular pointed crown, a fitted purple body covering, a dark navy full-face hood with two large pale-blue eye shapes, and a sweeping midnight-blue cape. a purple collar or facing rises into pointed ends around the shoulders. at the chest, a circular pale-blue medallion bears a purple m. the navy hoof boots are outlined in blue, with curved horizontal stripes like overlapping wraps. in the unmasked reveal, Twilight wears the same characteristic hat, clasp, cape and striped footwear. different friends take turns portraying the same hero, including Fluttershy's flying appearance. the coordinated costumes hide their identities and make them look like one recognizable character. my interpretation is that the strong two-color contrast, repeated chest emblem and concealed face are a masterclass in making an instantly legible superhero identity. i will not attribute the particular costume design to a real-world inspiration without direct production evidence.

### S2-06 — Twilight Sparkle's birthday dress, worn simple version

Twilight's finished birthday dress. a soft lemon-yellow, almost tunic-like garment hangs simply over the back, leaving the forelegs and tail unobstructed. broad rounded pink neck edging ties into a generous bow at the chest, with two pointed ends. a narrow cream or white edge finishes the lower hem. there are no great jewel borders or dramatic trailing layers. the gift is inspired by gratitude, and Twilight appreciates its simplicity. to my eye, the pink bow does nearly all the focal work. this might be the strongest argument in Rarity's portfolio that restraint can be as distinctive as extravagance.

### S2-08f — Rarity's own taffeta cape

Rarity's own ruffled taffeta cape. unlike the promised copies, this one is visible: a bright pink fabric draped from the upper body backward, with a dark magenta standing collar, pale pink curling neck ornaments and a light blue clasp. during the rescue it becomes an improvised sling and tears, so don't treat that distorted shape as the designed silhouette. taffeta is the confirmed textile. to me, this is a beautiful example of a single bold color carried by volume and texture rather than by an elaborate printed motif.

### S2-11 — fire-ruby necklace

the fire-ruby necklace. at Rarity's throat is a conspicuous faceted heart-shaped red stone with orange-red highlights, framed by a thick golden-yellow rim on a smooth gold-colored neck band. Spike supplies the ruby; the metalwork isn't specifically credited to Rarity. my reading is that the setting behaves almost like a frame around a painting. it is quiet enough that the stone is the entire focus. the necklace also carries the emotional inspiration that helped unlock her cape project.

### S2-10 — “Dreamboat Special”

the Dreamboat Special. yes, an actual named Rarity hairpiece! Pinkie commissions a replacement toupee for Cranky Doodle Donkey. instead of his earlier dark wig, picture a tall golden-blond pompadour, swept dramatically backward to a point, with curved lock lines, a pale yellow highlight and shorter pointed locks behind the ears. a little curved lock appears near the forehead. we don't know the fibers or fastenings. my interpretation is that the high silhouette and strong sweep project confidence: the design changes the whole character of his profile without needing a single piece of clothing.

### S2-W02 — revised bridal gown specification

the revised bridal gown for the disguised bride. the imposter asks for more beads and a longer train. in the imposter's wedding appearance, a broad white skirt is marked by thick yellow-gold curls in horizontal bands, gold decoration at the chest, gold hoof shoes, and a long rear sweep. a translucent veil falls from a wreath of alternating turquoise-and-white flowers. this is not proof that two separate finished dresses were made. my reading is that the scrollwork and elongated silhouette emphasize ceremony and spectacle, very much in line with the revision request.

### S2-W03 — Cadance's genuine wedding ensemble

Cadance's genuine wedding gown. here the palette is white and cream, with warm golden scroll-like decoration at the shoulder and chest, a turquoise accent near the neck and pointed or scalloped gold-colored shoes. a translucent veil flows from pale yellow and cream rose-like blossoms gathered at the base of her horn. her natural pink, purple and cream mane remains visible. the back seam and full train dimensions are not confirmed. this is the real bride's ensemble, distinct from the imposter's wreath styling. i read the softer flowers and gold accents as a lovely way of framing the face without making the entire dress compete with Cadance's natural colors.

### S2-W10 — Rarity's own bridesmaid dress

Rarity's own bridesmaid dress. a bright cyan drape with pale polka dots tapers to a pointed train, topped with a pink petal-shaped dotted overlay. a mint-green ribbon circles the neck, carrying a pink diamond-shaped ornament. on her head, a light aqua band supports green rosette-like flowers with pink centers. the forelegs are bare. it's such a clear composition: two large contrasting color areas, linked by repeated pale dots and floral headwear. i would read the pointed train as an elegant alternative to the huge rounded bridal skirt.

### S4-01 — signature Fashion Week textile

the original Manehattan Fashion Week textile. here is a design in its own right, before the dresses are even cut. the fabric is a mauve or plum-colored surface covered in little light-colored spiral curls. Rarity says it took months to develop; it stretches without clinging and has a controlled shimmer. no particular fiber or weave is established. i find the tiny repeated curls especially characteristic: they give the fabric movement on a small scale, while the material's actual behavior gives the whole garment freedom to move. this is Rarity as textile developer, not just decorator.

### S4-03 — “Hotel Chic”

Hotel Chic. with her original collection compromised, Rarity builds a replacement from the available hotel-room textiles and furnishings, with her friends helping construct it. it wins the competition. imagine the design vocabulary suggested by an elegant room: drapery that sweeps across a body, oversized tie-back-like bows, decorative bands, tassel-like forms and distinctive hats. the exact source of every material is not verified. the later official fashion short shows a board of sketches, including a large pink-purple pony study wearing a tall lavender hat, a huge green bow at the neck, a narrow vertical front ornament and a long teal scalloped train. aqua, mint, mustard and purple accessory trials appear along the board. note that those are design studies, not a guaranteed count of finished runway garments. the stated inspiration is the hotel itself; my interpretation is that Rarity has transformed interior-design rhythms into wearable silhouettes.

### S4-H01 — Hotel Chic concept thumbnail a

Hotel Chic concept one, the long drape. on the official retrospective board, a light-aqua pony sketch has a small, layered high-neck or shoulder piece, a short body band and a long gray fabric drape gathered behind the haunches, beneath the paler shoulder fabric. the head detail sweeps upward. the aqua is the illustrated pony color, not necessarily the garment. the composition is a study in contrast: a relatively compact front and a long soft rear. it suggests hanging curtains or other interior drapery, but that comparison is my interpretation, not an identified material assignment.

### S4-H02 — Hotel Chic concept thumbnail b

Hotel Chic concept two, the banded skirt. on a pale-mint model sketch, a dark bow marks the neck. a jacket-like short top meets a compact rounded rear skirt divided by contrasting horizontal bands. the full final runway palette is not verified. i read this as a more tailored and rhythmic alternative to concept one's flowing drape. the broad bands make the rear volume feel organized, much as decorative borders organize a room's textiles.

### S4-H03 — Hotel Chic concept thumbnail c

Hotel Chic concept three, the top-hat look. a violet illustrated pony wears a tall gray-purple hat that flares toward the top. the chest has a white shirtfront-like area with a large contrasting bow, and a dark ornament at the side. it's a vertical silhouette, quite different from the more rounded skirt concepts. the hat reminds me of a lampshade, but there is no verified one-to-one material identification. what we can actually see is a dramatic high hat and a formal shirtfront effect.

### S4-H04 — Hotel Chic concept thumbnail d

Hotel Chic concept four, the rounded skirt. a pale-yellow model sketch wears a short fitted upper section, a dark ribbon-like band and a large rounded skirt with pale circular or floral markings. there is a circular detail near the mane. much of the fine construction remains unresolved. where the previous design emphasizes the hat, this one seems to distribute its interest across the rounded skirt surface. the sketch offers a different balance of large silhouette and small repeating pattern.

### S4-11 — Rarity's rustic self-presentation / fashion demonstration

Rarity's fancy country styling. in a clear view, she wears an enormous pale-yellow woven-looking Western hat, with an ochre edge, little curved straw-like marks and a wide hot-pink band made of lighter horizontal stripes. cyan, magenta and purple round decorations cluster on the crown and around the brim. pale cloth near the chest and flank has bright pink scalloped edging and scattered pink, purple and blue dots. the full skirt and maker of the hat remain uncertain. i love the contradiction here: even when Rarity attempts rustic style, she turns the hat into a jewel-like focal object. this is not proof she personally fabricated every component.

### S5-05 — “Over the Moon”

Over the Moon. one of the most wonderfully specific gowns in the collection. the upper chest is almost-black indigo, with a purple high neck band, little white pearl-like circles around the edge, a white crescent moon and smaller four-pointed stars. dark rounded shoulder ornaments curl inward in visible spirals, like rosettes, edged with lavender scallops. a purple bow sits high behind the neckline, not at the waist, and a line of little white dots follows the rear edge of the fitted chest panel. the skirt rises over the back, then flows into long blue-violet layers with dark curved fold lines and scattered white dots and star-shaped sparkles. at the bottom is a dense band of irregular angular aqua and mint shapes resembling faceted gemstones. dark violet shoes repeat white crescents, small turquoise dots and curling lines. Rarity explicitly draws inspiration from Luna raising the moon. i read the turquoise hem as a visual counterweight to the tightly decorated shoulders: the dark field between them gives the little stars room to shine. the specific fibers, pearl material and mineral identities are not established.

### S5-06 — “The Reign in Stain”, renamed “Princess Dress”

The Reign in Stain, marketed as the Princess Dress. the front is a pointed deep-teal chestpiece with a sharp v-shaped arrangement and little round pale ornaments inside dark outlined cells. behind the shoulder rise white feather-like costume pieces edged in icy aqua. the front legs remain bare. the skirt begins with mint and aqua panels, passes into brighter blue, and finishes in lavender and violet, all flowing into a long rear train. the tiers have broad, irregular scalloped or petal-shaped edges. dark gently curved lines divide those panels like the leading of a stained-glass window, with little circular green, blue and white jewel-like nodes where the lines meet and inside the cells. the inspiration is explicitly the window commemorating Twilight's coronation. sassy changes the name to Princess Dress. what i find brilliant is the way the same theme works at multiple scales: the angular front, the large curved colored panels, the tiny round accents. it's not merely a window picture pasted onto a dress. the window's organization has become the dress's visual structure. that doesn't mean the garment is made from actual glass.

### S5-08 — standardized Princess Dress production run

the standardized Princess Dress production run. again we have that deep-teal angular chest, feather-like aqua shoulder details, scalloped stained-glass panels and long cool-colored train. the difference is not a new visual concept but a demand for exact repetition. Rarity is pressed into making many copies. my reading is that this is a story about creative labor: the best-known design can become the one that leaves the designer the least room to design.

### S5-11 — Rarity's Shadow Spade detective look

Rarity's Shadow Spade detective look. the visible jacket is a muted brick-red or burgundy, closely fitted with a standing collar, small dark button-like marks and gathered cuff details. a salmon-pink bow sits at the throat, and a coordinating hat is partly outside the inspected frame. Rarity says that she is channeling Shadow Spade through her clothes and later describes the adventure as showcasing Femme Mystique Chic, so the collection association is established. we still cannot identify this jacket with a specific one of the three opening mannequin gowns. to my eye, the close jacket and bow concentrate attention near the face, giving the outfit a smart, purposeful character distinct from her sweeping royal gowns.

### S5-15 — “Masquerade”

Masquerade. Rarity's named look combines a simple near-black or charcoal dress and an elaborate mask. the dress has a narrow curved neck band, a smooth close upper section, an opening for the wing and a long uninterrupted dark rear drape. the mask's exact markings remain unresolved. my reading is that the original pairing concentrates drama around the face while keeping the dress deliberately quiet. it is an elegant example of how a single ornate accessory can define an otherwise restrained outfit.

### S5-16 — Masquerade, dress-only configuration

Masquerade, the dress-only configuration. Fluttershy chooses the same black dress without the ornate mask because the mask restricts her peripheral vision. we still have that narrow dark neckline, smooth front, wing opening and uninterrupted rear drape. this is not a new underlying gown. what's especially interesting is how removing just one accessory changes both the function and the mood of the design. the wearer makes a practical decision without discarding the entire outfit.

### S5-17 — Rarity's mermaid costume

Rarity's mermare costume. a turquoise-to-blue fish-tail extension projects behind her, tapering to a point with a purple fin. little pale green shell-like shapes, yellow-white dots and short scale-like marks decorate the blue-green surface. her violet hair is swept into an ornate style with a pale mint shell-like decoration and small white bead-like dots near the forehead. this is a visual costume, not an actual seapony transformation. the tail swings behind her as she moves. my reading is that the aquatic motifs are an especially nice alternative to her usual faceted gems, while the long exaggerated tail transforms the outline of the pony. the specific textile and the individual making credit for her own outfit are not independently established.

### S5-18 — Twilight Sparkle's Nightmare Night costume

Twilight Sparkle's ancient-warrior-style Nightmare Night costume. imagine a bright gold helmet with cheek guards and a high, curved red crest marked by narrow vertical divisions; her horn protrudes at the front. a yellow-gold breastplate has a pointed shield-like center with curling decoration, over a deep blue-violet neck covering. at the rear, overlapping pointed gold panels carry little red dots, with pale fabric showing beneath. gold bands and shield-shaped leg guards ornament the legs. Rarity's group costume credit is supported by her dialogue. the historical-warrior comparison is my visual interpretation, not a verified real-world model from a production artist.

### S5-19 — Applejack's Nightmare Night costume

Applejack's lion costume. a thick reddish-brown shaggy mane frames her face, with little rounded triangular ears at the top and her blond forelock visible beneath. her body is covered by a smooth tan-brown costume, and the front legs end in shaggy reddish-brown cuffs and pale paw-like covers with short dark claw marks. the warm tawny palette is unified by the darker mane. my reading is that the design creates a recognizable animal with only a few high-impact shapes, particularly the oversized mane and paws. i won't assign a specific film character as the production inspiration without an artist's confirmation.

### S5-20 — Pinkie Pie's Nightmare Night costume

Pinkie Pie's roller-skating costume. two enormous round hot-pink hair puffs rise on either side of her head, above a pale aqua visor. her short pale-aqua top has bright blue-green edging; a purple lower garment is edged with white and mint. pale aqua and purple striped legwear leads into light mint roller skates with dark purple wheels, bright cuffs, and little purple bows. matching protective-looking cuffs continue the color scheme. my interpretation is that the exaggerated round puffs, strong horizontal stripes and repeated cool-color trim produce a playful retro athletic look. the episode establishes Rarity's group costume association, not a confirmed real-world decade or fashion reference.

### S5-21 — Rainbow Dash's Nightmare Night costume

Rainbow Dash's astronaut costume. a round transparent-looking bubble helmet is edged in mint green, with a pale curved head covering inside, leaving pointed ear shapes visible. the outfit is white and pale mint with darker green outlining. two round disc-like ornaments sit on the chest harness, set against green geometric line patterns; several green curved bands wrap the torso. the pale hoof boots have mint outlines and round mechanical-looking accents. her blue wings and rainbow tail remain visible. i read the circular helmet and repeated disc shapes as a unified futuristic visual language. the astronaut theme is obvious in the frame, but a resemblance to a particular movie character is not evidence of artist intent.

### S7-11 — punk self-reinvention

Rarity's punk transformation. what a spectacular break from her usual silhouette. her mane becomes long pointed sweeping locks in mint green, deep purple and bright yellow. a dark eggplant-purple fitted sleeveless jacket has a high sharp collar and an open front showing her white chest. pale blue-white round studs decorate the collar and curved arm opening. a darker vertical strap ends in a light rectangular silver-colored buckle, and a matching dark hoof cuff carries pale circular studs. a dark studded band gathers the short multicolored tail; pale blue eye shadow and dark lashes complete the styling. the most recent frame check confirmed the jacket, collar, studs, buckle and mane in particular; not every tail detail was reverified. this is the response to her hair mishap, a self-created fashion identity, although it doesn't prove she sewed the jacket from scratch. my reading is that the transformation retains Rarity's strengths—color harmony, carefully repeated ornament and attention to silhouette—but expresses them through points, studs and asymmetry rather than gold scrollwork and soft curls. that's why it feels like her, even when she looks completely different.

### MOV-01 — Capper's coat restoration

Capper's coat restoration, from the 2017 pony movie. here we get another beautifully concrete design object: a long burgundy or red-brown tailored coat, with a raised pointed collar, fitted long sleeves, dark cuffs, an open front and pointed lower tails. Rarity repairs the torn sleeve-cuff seam and adds two round gold-colored buttons, one on each lapel, that contrast with the dark red surface. the coat is fitted to an upright cat, not a four-legged pony, and its existing pattern is not attributed to Rarity. my interpretation is that the buttons are the smallest possible intervention with an enormous visual effect. two well-placed gold points can restore definition and dignity to worn clothing. the real accomplishment is understanding what to preserve rather than automatically replacing the whole garment.

### S9-Y02 — Yona's finished Amity Ball dress

Yona's finished Amity Ball dress. strong green fabric drapes around her rounded, shaggy yak body, with a darker green band and pale aqua accents. an oversized bright-blue flower with a golden-yellow center sits at the side near the band. much of her natural body is covered, but her horns and feet remain visible. the matching makeover adds a massive swept purple-and-magenta wig and pale aqua round earrings. we don't know the precise fabric of the green dress. the large flower is a strong focal point against the darker green. yet my reading of the full makeover is critical: the design prioritizes the appearance of pony formality, instead of discovering an elegant expression of Yona's own identity. that tension is central to the episode.

### S9-Y03 — Yona's wig and pony-style grooming

Yona's wig and pony-style grooming. a huge purple hairstyle with a magenta stripe sweeps over the head, accompanied by round aqua earrings and blue-green cosmetic accents. the natural horns remain visible. these are styling interventions within the ball project, not evidence of another dress or another textile. i find the hair especially telling: it changes the apparent profile of the client as much as the gown does. a successful makeover should make someone feel more themselves, not simply make them resemble the designer's existing idea of a formal pony.

### S9-04 — Twilight's final coronation gown

Twilight's final coronation gown. here is Rarity's culminating royal commission, distinct from the first coronation and the retail Princess Dress. the front is lavender or periwinkle-blue with a folded icy-blue diagonal sash. at the breast is a golden-yellow star-shaped ornament with a vivid magenta starburst at its center. a white or pale lavender gathered band curves over the back behind the wing. the skirt stretches rearward in lavender panels, with three visible pale many-pointed stars near the wing and darker purple, curved, overlapping folds toward the rear. a thick light-blue border follows the lower train, and pale ice-white hoof coverings have pointed, crown-like tops. the far end of the train is cropped in the checked frame. Twilight's raised striped ponytail is ceremony styling, not a separately credited Rarity accessory. my reading is that the star motif has matured with its wearer: the little stars of the first Gala dress become a strong central emblem and a few carefully placed accents. the restrained cool palette and long silhouette emphasize succession and ceremony rather than a generic princess fantasy.

### FIF-01 — Twilight's completed primary coronation gown

the completed primary coronation gown, from A-Dressing Memories. Rarity confirms that the actual dress had been finished weeks earlier. it is the lavender and periwinkle design with the icy-blue sash, star emblem, white gathered back detail and long star-decorated train that we just heard about. this is a continuity clarification, not a second new gown. the fitting in the later-produced story concerns a separate backup. i particularly like this record because it gives us evidence of a designer planning ahead for a major ceremony.

### FIF-02 — Twilight's backup coronation gown

Twilight's backup coronation gown. now this really is a different design. desaturated slate-blue and teal dominate, with pale aqua and icy-blue accents. a close front piece has small rounded scallops along its lower edge. the long rear skirt consists of several broad, vertically hanging rounded panels with deeper blue shading toward their upper edges. a pale blue-white drape crosses over the back and drops in a long vertical panel at the side. the emphasis is on rounded contours and the contrast between that pale drape and the darker skirt, rather than the visible star placement of the primary gown. a measuring tape in the fitting is a tool, not part of the finished decoration. i read the backup as a quieter, more tonal interpretation of royal dress. we can see the distinct color and shape arrangement, but the exact fibers and closures remain unknown.

### SH-04 — Hotel Chic retrospective

the Hotel Chic retrospective. this revisits the hotel-inspired collection and the design process we discussed earlier: draped forms, a tall hat, oversized bow studies, striped or scalloped panels and color trials. the four thumbnail studies and larger drawing are not independently new collections. the short uses Hotel Chic to discuss style and function together. it adds valuable design-board evidence to our existing record, rather than increasing the number of unique finished gowns.

### WARD-04 — Suited For Success

in Suited For Success, the workroom glasses and measuring tape are practical tools, not dress ornament. the first fashion-show appearance and the completed rose-and-gold Gala gown document Rarity as both working designer and wearer. for the latter, remember the layered plum-edged skirt, gold swags and pink-stoned tiara.

### WARD-08 — The Best Night Ever

in The Best Night Ever, the finished Gala ensemble returns: broad rose panels edged in plum, gold swags, a long train, a tiara and polished mane. this is the same collaborative finished design from the first runway, not another gown.

### WARD-11 — Secret of My Excess

in Secret of My Excess, Rarity's taffeta cape is a strong pink-magenta rear drape with a gathered edge. this is the one that belongs to the named-material cape project, not a different unnamed outerwear collection.

### WARD-16 — A Canterlot Wedding – part 2

in A Canterlot Wedding, part two, Rarity's bridesmaid dress has bright cyan dotted drapery, a pointed train, a pink dotted petal overlay and mint-green neck ribbon with a pink diamond-shaped accent. her green floral headpiece has pink centers. this returns us to the documented group commission.

### WARD-27 — Rarity Investigates!

in Rarity Investigates, the detective outfit and the formalwear express the Shadow Spade theme. the checked detective view shows brick-red or burgundy jacket fabric, a standing collar, dark button-like marks and a salmon bow. the royal dinner gown's precise identification remains unresolved; do not confuse the two looks.

### WARD-28 — Scare Master

in Scare Master, her mermare look uses a turquoise-to-blue tail with a purple fin, pale shell-like decorations and tiny scale marks, and a violet updo with a mint shell-like accent and bead-like dots. it uses creature transformation as the central visual concept. the exact fabric and personal maker credit remain unknown.

## appendix — reference-only designs and incomplete physical descriptions

these 178 records remain available in the full catalogue, but are not separate spoken design readings in the visual-only edition. the original evidence qualifications are preserved.

### S1-07 — school-play costumes, gem-embellished revision

the gemstone-revised school-play costumes from Rarity’s childhood. after discovering the gems hidden inside the rock, Rarity returns to her costumes and decorates them with colored stones. we can't confidently enumerate each stone or its position. what we can say is that the embellishment is her breakthrough. the costumes become more visually compelling without requiring a completely different underlying brief. this is the beginning of her signature: light, color and precious-looking details used to elevate an existing garment.

### S1-08 — Sapphire Shores' jewel-encrusted show costume

Sapphire Shores' diamond stage costume. a celebrity commission, and one of the clearest examples of Rarity's extravagant use of gemstones. the costume is explicitly covered in diamonds. the audited reference does not establish the unveiled garment's exact cut or base color, and the outfit Sapphire wears when she enters the boutique is not automatically that design. on stage, the obvious intended effect is a strong concentration of sparkle. the challenge is creating something that will read under performance conditions rather than only at arm's length.

### S1-11 — Fluttershy's boutique photoshoot wardrobe

Fluttershy's boutique photoshoot wardrobe. in Green Isn't Your Color, Rarity fits her model in clothing for Photo Finish. Rarity herself says the headdress is too large for Fluttershy and the cape is too sparkly. Photo Finish subsequently prefers a simpler look inspired by nature and criticizes the previous sparkles and feathers. so we have genuine evidence of a large headpiece, a sparkly cape, and feather ornamentation in the initial styling, even if we cannot securely assign each color or feather to a particular component. my reading is that the photographer and designer are looking at the same model with very different priorities: one favors the garment's spectacle, the other the model's natural presence. Photo Finish's later clothes are not automatically Rarity originals.

### S2-F03 — orange monochrome outfit

the orange Full Spectrum outfit. a broad bright-orange headpiece, an orange-gold short garment at the front, a pale yellow square or diamond-like ornament and a light yellow cuff are visible. other mannequins obscure much of it. to my eye, the golden shapes create a warm, luminous impression without having to introduce a completely different hue. that's a visual reading, not evidence of an actual metal or gemstone.

### S2-F04 — yellow monochrome outfit

the yellow Full Spectrum outfit. large circular orange-colored lenses set inside pale-yellow frames are the clearest feature, with yellow and lime accents visible on the partially hidden figure. we can't establish a complete skirt or accessory set. what makes the surviving detail interesting is scale: those oversized circles could carry a whole visual identity. the monochromatic theme remains the documented collection idea.

### S2-F05 — purple/magenta monochrome outfit

the purple and magenta Full Spectrum outfit. at the far side of the mannequin line, we can make out curved and pointed pink-purple ornamentation. the rest is largely hidden. my impression is of a stronger interplay between curves and points than in the round blue accessories, but i won't assign a neckline, skirt cut or exact purple palette that we cannot see. this is the partially documented edge of the collection.

### S2-02a — unnamed baby-blue sapphire client ensemble

the baby-blue sapphire ensemble, from Sisterhooves Social. this is an editorial description, not a retail name. Rarity explicitly needs unusually rare pale-blue sapphires for an important client's outfit. later she is almost finished with the ensemble and needs one more gem. the pale-blue gemstones are established by dialogue, but i cannot specify the entire garment's base color, stone count, neckline, or arrangement from that alone. i particularly like how this story demonstrates the importance of the smallest element in a design: one missing ornament can keep a project unfinished, yet Rarity's discovery of the drawing reminds her that the stones have an emotional value beyond their intended decorative use. the client's identity and finished delivery are unknown. this is a documented commission, not a new invented design.

### S2-03 — Opalescence's sweater

Opalescence's shrunken sweater. a designer sweater made of crocheted wool shrinks in the wash and ends up fitting the cat. its original designer is not established, and the color and stitch arrangement aren't securely described in our reference. this is an accidental size transformation rather than a deliberate petwear design. for a fashion designer, it's a reminder that a textile's behavior in washing can completely change the fit and purpose of a garment.

### S2-08 — ruffled taffeta cape collection

the ruffled taffeta cape collection. Rarity researches earlier fashions, anticipates the return of ruffled capes and finds renewed inspiration in Spike's gift of a fire ruby. taffeta is explicitly named, as is the gathered or ruffled cape idea. we do not have five verified finished colorways for her friends. the design emphasis is the contrast between the broad fall of fabric and the gathered edge. here fashion history and the emotional impact of a gemstone both feed a new line.

Applejack's bridesmaid dress. a cool aqua-green floral wreath and coordinated neck ornament are visible against her orange coat and blond mane. the complete back panel and pattern are not securely established. within the bridal party, the shared floral vocabulary ties her to the other attendants. my reading is that those cool accessories provide an effective contrast to her naturally warm coloring without asking her to abandon her own recognizable character.

the brown dress imposed by Trixie. in Magic Duel, Rarity objects to a brown-dominated outfit placed on her by magic. it is explicitly not her creation, and our reference does not verify every trim detail. its role is almost the reverse of a designer's personal signature: somebody else imposes a look she dislikes. keep it in the visual archive as a contrast, not a garment from her portfolio.

the original Fashion Week clothing line. further Hotel Chic runway views. there are more angles and design studies, but the four thumbnails we just heard about are not securely matched one by one to every finalized runway look. remember that large study with the lavender hat, huge green bow and teal scalloped train; its multiple angles are a development process, not multiple new gowns. for a designer, this is an important distinction: a front view, a side view and a color trial may all belong to one garment.

Small Town Chic. Spike's crystal suit. this is a rigid, gemstone-like covering rather than a flexible, conventionally tailored suit. it is cumbersome enough to immobilize him; a full inventory of its colors and facet shapes isn't established. it is made magically, not by Rarity's ordinary sewing methods. imagine ornament becoming the entire structure rather than an accent. this is a very direct critique of the idea that increasing the amount of precious-looking material necessarily improves a design.

the remaining magical furniture, chariots and rooftops. these are further examples of the spell-driven transformations, not a count of individual Rarity dresses. the broad language is ornate shapes, gold-colored effects, jewel-like decoration and often enlarged scale. the individual objects aren't all inventoried. for our fashion podcast, the takeaway is that embellishment should have a hierarchy and a purpose; the spell removes that restraint.

the oversized fabric dress reproduction. the next command produces a very large garment. the underlying design is still copied from the book; the documented change is scale. no precise color, size or construction measurements are verified. my interpretation is that fit is not a secondary detail that can be fixed by making everything bigger or smaller. it's fundamental to whether a garment can function. Yona's trial makeover concepts. during the song, we see a series of alternatives associated with curly, blue, retro, contemporary, Twilight-like and furry styling. those are descriptive labels, not official design names or six verified finished garments. we cannot match each fabric mentioned in the fitting to an individual montage frame or assign a complete palette and pattern. what the sequence reveals is the breadth of Rarity's experimentation and the risk of starting with preconceived styles instead of asking which style feels most natural to Yona.

the castle tapestry research. in Castle Mane-ia, Rarity is interested in historic textiles and the castle's furnishings. this is a research activity, not a documented finished dress collection. what appeals to me is the way an old decorative object can become a source of motifs, borders or surface treatments for a later designer. we should stop short of claiming that any specific Rarity gown came from a particular tapestry unless the episode makes the connection.

in Power Ponies, the superhero appearance is Radiance, in the comic-book world. the original costume designer is not Rarity simply because she inhabits the character. exact design details aren't verified in this source. the superhero role offers a different silhouette and visual language from her normal pony wardrobe.

### WARD-21 — Rarity Takes Manehattan

in Rarity Takes Manehattan, her travel, city and runway appearances form the wider wardrobe around the fashion competition. Hotel Chic and the original curled textile are discussed in detail in the main program; separate personal looks remain unverified in full. fashion is part of how she moves through the city as a professional.

### WARD-23 — For Whom the Sweetie Belle Toils

in For Whom the Sweetie Belle Toils, Rarity's boutique and theatre-related appearances are part of the wider costume-making story. the individual personal garments are not fully described or attributed in the catalogue. it is useful to see the designer in a backstage context rather than assuming every outfit belongs to the stage commission.

### WARD-24 — Inspiration Manifestation

in Inspiration Manifestation, the magical appearances reflect the enchanted transformation of her design practice. they are not ordinary commissioned garments, and their individual visual specifications are unresolved. the sequence is a study of excess and the loss of practical restraint.

### WARD-25 — Make New Friends but Keep Discord

in Make New Friends but Keep Discord, Rarity's second Gala outfit is a separate visual occasion from the first Gala. no full independent specification or designer credit is established here. it should not be merged with the rose-and-gold first gown just because both belong to a Gala.

### WARD-26 — Canterlot Boutique

in Canterlot Boutique, the opening and workroom styling show Rarity in her professional setting. the individual outfits aren't all verified as original authored designs. the difference between wearing a garment to present a boutique and designing the entire boutique's inventory is worth preserving.

### WARD-29 — The Cutie Re-Mark

in The Cutie Re-Mark, the alternate wartime appearance places Rarity in uniform-making work. the clothing's exact specifications are unverified, and the events are in an alternate timeline. the context makes functionality, production and labor much more prominent than courtly ornament.

### WARD-32 — A Hearth's Warming Tail

in A Hearth's Warming Tail, Rarity appears as a fictional character within the episode's story. this is a theatrical character costume, not automatically an original boutique design. the exact palette and construction aren't verified in the catalogue.

### WARD-33 — The Cart Before the Ponies

in The Cart Before the Ponies, the mechanic outfit accompanies her work on the racer. the full palette, cut and authorship remain unresolved. the important difference from a Gala look is the visual language of work: clothing identifies what role the character is playing.

### WARD-34 — P.P.O.V. (Pony Point of View)

in Pony Point of View, the different seafaring accounts include extravagant and elegant nautical looks. their full visual specifications are not confirmed, and the different accounts should not be combined into one garment. in each retelling, appearance is part of how a narrator remembers or dramatizes the same experience.

### WARD-35 — Forever Filly

in Forever Filly, the paired costumes return: Bo Peep and sheep, chicken and egg, butterfly and caterpillar, frog and tadpole, flower and bud. each relationship supplies a shared idea expressed through two different forms. we don't have verified palettes or individual authorship; the main program treats each pair separately.

### WARD-36 — Honest Apple

in Honest Apple, Rarity's competition-related styling is a personal appearance, apart from the entrants' collections. exact personal garment specifications are unverified. the episode positions her as a judge and professional colleague as much as a designer.

### WARD-37 — Fame and Misfortune

in Fame and Misfortune, the stress couture appearance shows a different side of self-presentation. the precise design details and maker aren't established. wardrobe can make a state of mind visible, even when the look is deliberately less composed than usual.

### WARD-39 — Shadow Play – part 2

in Shadow Play, part two, the square-dancing outfit is an occasion-specific appearance. its colors, trim and maker aren't independently confirmed. dancing offers an interesting functional brief, because the costume has to contribute to the scene in motion as well as in a still frame.

### WARD-40 — film and publicity

in the 2017 movie, Rarity's pony, travel and pirate-associated appearances provide a wider visual wardrobe. their individual design specifications are not established as her creations. the seapony transformation is a change of physical form, not a garment. Capper's burgundy coat restoration is the clearly credited clothing intervention from the film.

### WARD-41 — School Daze – part 1

in School Daze, part one, the Generosity teacher appearance establishes her new professional role. we do not have a separately attributed complete garment specification. it belongs to the record of how she presents herself outside the boutique.

### WARD-42 — Friendship University

in Friendship University, the Plainity disguise changes her recognizable identity for the investigation. the precise costume and colors need independent verification. the visual purpose, unlike her usual couture, is to avoid being recognized.

### WARD-44 — Sparkle's Seven

in Sparkle's Seven, the royal-guard armor disguise is a role-based appearance. its exact color, components and maker aren't independently specified in our archive. like Plainity, its design purpose in the scene is disguise; it is not an established line of armor manufactured by Rarity.

### WARD-45 — She's All Yak

in She's All Yak, Rarity's Amity Ball outfit belongs to the formal event surrounding Yona's makeover. the full personal garment details and authorship are unresolved. it is a visual reference distinct from the clearly documented green drape and blue flower worn by Yona.

### WARD-46 — Dragon Dropped

in Dragon Dropped, there are three appearances to locate: the first spelunking look, the Mane-iac costume and the second spelunking look. we do not have verified full colors or cuts for each. the two cave-exploration looks belong to a practical activity, while the character costume belongs to shared fictional interests. the change of brief is the important distinction.

### WARD-47 — The Last Problem

finally, in The Last Problem, Rarity's later-life look and coronation-preparation styling mark two points in her story. the individual garments aren't fully specified or independently attributed. her final royal commission, by contrast, is the well-documented lavender star gown we've already discussed. the personal appearances give the designer herself a place in the visual archive without confusing her wardrobe with her authored work.

*end of transcript and appendix.*


## final radio-alignment audit (not spoken)



- Gala gowns: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Suited_For_Success) confirms the five personality-inspired gifts and friends following Rarity's design for her gown; [episode gallery](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Suited_For_Success/Gallery) and [fashion-show frame](https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x6f3q1b) support selected visual details. Pinkie's dress was a gift, not a paid commission.
- Full Spectrum: [dialogue](https://www.springfieldspringfield.co.uk/view_episode_scripts.php?episode=s02e05&tv-show=my-little-pony-friendship-is-magic) confirms the name and Sweetie Belle's role. detailed colorways retain the earlier catalogue's visual evidence.
- Mare Do Well: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/The_Mysterious_Mare_Do_Well) explicitly confirms Rarity made the costumes and Fluttershy flew in one. shortened the radio title to the hero's name, rather than an episode title.
- birthday dress: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Sweet_and_Elite) confirms Twilight liked its simplicity; removed the unsupported implication of a planned, completed final specification.
- taffeta cape and ruby: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Secret_of_My_Excess), [cape frame](https://ponerpics.org/images/7459743), and [necklace frame](https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x3kxvqy) support the collar, curling pink decoration, blue clasp, heart-shaped ruby and broad gold neck band. the earlier slender necklace description was inaccurate. the ruby gift inspired the cape line; metalwork attribution is still uncertain.
- Dreamboat Special: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/A_Friend_in_Deed) confirms name, commission and maker.
- textile and Hotel Chic: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Rarity_Takes_Manehattan) confirms textile properties and line name; [in-universe sketch sheet from the official short](https://ponerpics.org/images/7135774) supports gray drapery, pale shoulder detail, contrasting bands, hat and skirt thumbnails. sketches are not treated as proof of final runway construction.
- Royal Regalia: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Canterlot_Boutique) confirms Luna's moon, Twilight's stained-glass window, and the full original title The Reign in Stain. a [presentation frame](https://fancaps.net/tv/picture.php?/3227300) supports the pointed chestpiece; earlier full visual descriptions retain their original evidence level.
- Femme Mystique Chic: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Rarity_Investigates!) confirms the line preceded the investigation and was inspired by Shadow Spade; Rarity described her adventure as a chance to showcase it.
- Nightmare Night: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/Scare_Master) explicitly describes Masquerade as a simple black dress with an ornate mask, and confirms group costume association. [costume frame](https://derpibooru.org/images/1149261) and [another angle](https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x3iy53t) support the warrior, lion, skater and astronaut palettes and silhouettes.
- Capper: [movie transcript](https://movies.fandom.com/wiki/My_Little_Pony%3A_The_Movie_(2017)/Transcript) describes the repaired sleeve cuff and one gold button on each lapel, rather than an unspecified row of buttons. the original coat pattern is not attributed to Rarity.
- Yona: [dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/She%27s_All_Yak) confirms her preference for brown and the Amity Ball context. the fashion criticism is Astra's interpretation.
- coronation: [preparation dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/The_Last_Problem), [backup fitting dialogue](https://mlp.fandom.com/wiki/Transcripts/A-Dressing_Memories), [ceremony frame](https://twibooru.org/2808492), [gown frame](https://twibooru.org/1743652), and [backup fitting frame](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt11447040/) support the two distinct looks. weeks-early completion and late planned sash adjustment are both retained; no claim that the backup was worn at the ceremony.

limits: transcripts are secondary transcriptions of canon dialogue and image hosts reproduce frames; no fan-created drawings or theories were used as garment evidence in this new pass. several gallery requests were blocked, and the other detailed designs were compared to the existing audited catalogue rather than independently reconstructed frame by frame. no claim of exhaustive independent visual certification is made. the existing reference-only group and 17 retired IDs are unchanged. episode and source names appear only in unspoken documentation. the closing line is user-specified, and presumes the catalogue is actually provided alongside the broadcasts.
