Rarity could imagine having a place of her own to get ready. Applejack knew how to build it. They were going to have opinions about every inch.

Spend enough time being the person people come to for help with animals and they can get the idea they know everything you’re good at. Sunset invited Fluttershy onto her gaming channel to introduce her to video games. Fluttershy picked one with squirrels. The idea was to collect nuts in a basket, and in short order Fluttershy was doing exceptionally well at it. Sunset, who had expected to spend the session explaining things, grew visibly frustrated. Eventually she settled in to watch Fluttershy play. By then the people tuning in to Sunset’s channel were getting to know both girls rather well.

Fluttershy choosing the squirrel game makes me smile. A friend may have an ability that our familiar picture of her has left out. It is a small delight to discover a new part of someone we thought we already knew rather well.

At one of Trixie’s street performances, Twilight saw a use for telekinesis that would have bewildered the examiners at Crystal Prep. A little real magic went into the act. She let Trixie keep the applause.

Expertise didn’t help much at the planetarium when Twilight found herself in the same room as Rosette Nebula, an astrophysicist she admired. She knew the science perfectly well. It was walking up and introducing herself that got her. Pinkie tried to help and managed to make being inconspicuous practically impossible. Later there was chocolate cake, and eventually Twilight did get to talk to Rosette. Pinkie naturally drew her own conclusions about the cake.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 16 · another year at canterlot

tracks.announcement_text:
The girls have been finding new ways to share their interests. Come with me, friend, to the Canterlot Pet Show.

Fluttershy sounded as if she were reading someone else’s handwriting when Applejack introduced her as cohost of the first annual Canterlot Pet Show. Then a Boston terrier barked. Fluttershy brightened. His name was Banana, he liked bananas, and he had a toy banana he was particularly fond of. Another dog confided a weakness for daytime television. The camera was still on, the audience still there, but Fluttershy had stopped thinking about what to say on camera. She wanted to know what the next dog had to say.

By the time Applejack needed to wind things up, Fluttershy was asking for one more interview. It was Winona. Apple Bloom had brought the family dog along to compete, a secret Winona herself had wanted to keep from Applejack. Fluttershy got to deliver the surprise and send them off together. She closed the broadcast herself.

The microphone had not grown less intimidating in the instant that the Boston terrier barked. Fluttershy had simply found someone she was interested in hearing. Her attention moved toward the little creature instead of toward the audience's judgment. I can appreciate that as a radio host, friend. There is a wonderful difference between wanting to be heard and having something one wants to share.

During the victory lap she had the inside word on Tank, who had helped Rainbow win second place despite being in love. Applejack looked impressed by the reporting. Apparently Tank was a chatty fellow if you happened to speak tortoise. Micro Chips and his robot took third. Cranky Doodle and his dog Fluffersnuff won, a fine comeback by a dog whose mood during the personality round had left something to be desired. Gummy, Pinkie’s stuffed alligator, remained one competitor whose private thoughts Fluttershy could never quite get at.

Gummy had rather more to say when Pinkie supplied the voice herself. She recorded a cookie lesson in which Gummy praised her and helpfully reminded her to leave some chocolate chips for the dough. Tank attended as well. It was quite a feat for a tortoise to get near an ingredient before a girl who moved at Pinkie’s speed had whisked it away. She worked two kisses from him into the recipe and made sure he got a finished cookie.

Back at Twilight’s house, Spike had ordered a deluxe package of dog supplies for his own viewers. It included a flying disc much too delicate to throw and a used sock that Spike considered the highlight. Twilight had found the receipt. Two hundred dollars was a lot to spend on the pleasure of smelling someone’s foot. The items went back into the box, in front of the same audience that had just seen them come out.

There was room on the girls’ feeds for things that went wrong, too. Rainbow tried hiding in Pinkie’s locker to give her a scare and wound up as the frightened party. An attempt at a bottle flip could end with Principal Celestia showing the students how it was done. Rarity let people see the outtakes from her own song, and Applejack let them see hers. It gave you a rather different impression of somebody’s poise when you’d seen what happened before the take she kept.

Rarity even tried filming summer street fashion on an autumn day. Applejack, Fluttershy, and Rainbow all agreed to model. The clothes looked lovely. Their legs were cold. The arrival of snow settled a production decision for Rarity. She could make the next one indoors.

A dog chased a cat, Pinkie lost her balance with a tray of cupcakes, and Twilight’s coffee went flying. For most people on the sidewalk, those events belonged to the same untidy second. For Rainbow it was quite enough time to find the dog’s owner, put the cat in Fluttershy’s arms, steady Pinkie, arrange the cupcakes back on the tray, and send the coffee back into the cup.

You could understand why she sometimes got impatient. When Rainbow sang “Run to Break Free,” she described what it felt like to walk through school at everybody else’s pace. Even a perfectly agreeable afternoon stretched an awfully long way for a girl who could clear a truck in a single leap. Yet here she was using all that time to save someone a clean shirt. You could blink and come away with the impression that your coffee had behaved itself.

Rainbow's speed gives her time to do things that nobody else will even notice. I find that a much lovelier use of her extraordinary gift than winning another contest. Somewhere there is a girl going about her morning with absolutely no idea how close her coffee came to a very different destiny.

When Applejack asked Rainbow to help out on the farm, Rainbow took the assignment seriously. Unfortunately it was also the day A. K. Yearling was signing books. Rainbow could see her way clear to keeping both commitments if she allowed hardly any time for doing the chores. She ate up the work with her super speed. She hadn’t allowed for the Apples wanting to sit down over cider, and she couldn’t understand why Applejack seemed hurt when all the work was getting done.

Applejack and Big Mac could manage the farm. What they scarcely got to do anymore, given homework and the occasional emergency downtown, was spend an afternoon with Rainbow. The invitation had seemed quite clear from their end. Once Applejack found out about the signing, she went along to the bookstore. They were late for the event, but she caught Yearling on the way out. Rainbow got her book signed and the two girls still had the evening together. Next time she heard that a friend had some leaves that needed raking, she might want to leave the whole afternoon free.

What Applejack wanted was not a farm that had finished its work earlier than usual. She wanted the afternoon with Rainbow. The distinction is easily missed when one is trying very hard to be useful. A shared hour sometimes matters more than all the tasks that could have fitted into it.

The school later offered prizes for individual sports and one for the best athlete overall. Rainbow’s friends trained for different events. Fluttershy beat her at discus. Twilight beat her at ping-pong. Rarity had her in ballet. And so it went until Rainbow had a pile of second-place medals and a perfectly genuine claim on the overall title, which brought her surprisingly little comfort. It took an exhibition soccer match to draw her back out. She had advice about who to put where. Her friends could do some fairly spectacular things, especially once their captain started taking pleasure in how good they’d become.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 17 · the microphone and the afternoon

tracks.announcement_text:
There is a great deal of energy in Rainbow Dash. Let us follow her through a few of the adventures that put it to good use.

The invitation to play Blitzball at school came with one condition that stopped Rainbow cold. Coach Comet Chaser wanted boys only on his team. Rainbow challenged the league to play against the girls. She wanted any girl who could play to get an honest tryout. Once the match was under way, she noticed something odd about the opposition. They could barely keep going. Double practices for two weeks had done a remarkably good job of draining the pleasure out of their sport. Rainbow, ahead on points and in reach of what she’d come for, proposed that both sides call a tie. The coach walked out when his own players stood up to him. With help from a teacher, they could put together a school league where they had a say in how they played. As a route to getting on a team it was fairly involved. As an afternoon spent figuring out what a captain owed the other people on the field, Rainbow could hardly have done better.

Think back to another occasion after the Friendship Games. Canterlot High and Crystal Prep put on a joint science fair, and Twilight had the opportunity to work with students who remembered her as the girl with the private research project. This time she and her partner built a device to get people dancing. They tested it with Rarity and Pinkie, and the Rainbooms supplied an original song, “Get Up and Dance.” Fluttershy wanted the other students on backup vocals. At the demonstration even the principals got moving, a sight worth turning up for whatever you thought of the science. The project placed second. Plenty of people could say they’d had a hand in it, including the girl who wanted everybody else on the recording.

I like that Rainbow eventually sees the tired boys as people rather than as obstacles between her and the victory. Winning the right to participate is important. Making a game that everyone can enjoy is another accomplishment entirely. Her friends' science fair shows a similarly pleasant change in the meaning of a successful result.

Working together was a little harder on a shift at Sugarcube Corner. Pinkie liked the chance to tinker with a cupcake recipe and to know the person across the counter. When Rarity joined as cashier, the two friends discovered they had quite different ideas of good service. Then a chain bakery opened across the street. There was now a very practical reason to figure out what they could give a customer at their little shop that she couldn’t get by crossing the road. Friendship got them both behind the counter. The actual work of getting along had to happen there, one customer at a time.

At school, Rainbow had ten minutes before a championship soccer game against Crystal Prep and no idea where she’d put her lucky sock. Sunset tried to give the credit for Rainbow’s accomplishments to the person standing in front of her. Pinkie thought playing sockless sounded fine. Rainbow, who had to go out there with the team counting on her, would still quite like a sock.

My ears twitch with amusement. I do understand the comfort of a familiar little object before an important undertaking. But Rainbow has been carrying the skill she needs with her all along. I would not, however, recommend borrowing Bulk's sock.

Rarity could sew her a new one and set it with enough gems to briefly dazzle the opposing players when the sunlight hit them. Trixie had the advantage of a magician’s hat full of surprises. Give Rainbow Trixie’s lucky sock and the thing could take an active interest in directing her foot toward the winning shot. She could also borrow Bulk’s. He’d been preserving its luck by leaving it unwashed, which would do remarkable things for the amount of space everybody gave Rainbow on the pitch. Whichever sock she put on, it was Rainbow who had to keep her nerve long enough to score.

Rainbow Dash kept a tortoise named Tank. They went to the skate park together and recorded tricks. Set that beside the guitar solos, the soccer games, her delight in Daring Do, and the look she could get when somebody said an activity was too difficult, and it becomes possible to predict how she’d spend a spring-break cruise. She had six friends with extraordinary powers, an ocean of possibilities, and very little interest in the concept of time off.

Her friends had distinctly more interest. Applejack would have been happy just to get her stomach to agree with the motion of the ship. Twilight thought there ought to be some stretch of water where a perfectly sound scientific explanation for an odd light could get a fair hearing. Rarity had even set a location alert on her phone for duty-free shopping. Rainbow heard it go off and thought they were under attack. It was going to be a long cruise.

On the Luxe Deluxe the girls filmed themselves singing “I’m on a Yacht.” Pinkie got a rap break, dolphins leaped, and there was plenty of room for a girl with a new outfit to let the wind catch it. They looked utterly pleased with themselves. It’s worth keeping that picture of the trip alongside the memory of the lifeboats. They had come on board with music and a plan to enjoy the sea.

Rainbow really did see something shining out at sea. Unfortunately she’d spent enough time looking for a menace that her honest account sounded much like her wishful thinking. By morning she’d taken a lifeboat and gone after it. Sunset and Twilight followed her to an island. They found her sinking into what looked like quicksand. Sunset discovered that the sand concealed a portal to Equestria.

There were now two girls experiencing pony legs for the first time in company with Sunset, the original pony who had long since got used to sneakers. Rainbow had wings to consider. Twilight had a horn. In Ponyville, Princess Twilight helped identify what Rainbow had seen. It was a trace of the Storm King’s magic, enough to put a ship in real danger.

Rainbow had to hear that it was tiring to be recruited into one of her adventures. Twilight had to live with the fact that a friend whose conclusion sounded ridiculous had made an accurate observation. With the ship in trouble, neither girl had much to gain from a long discussion of who’d been right first. They took the Storm King’s staff back through the portal and quelled the storm. The ship was still sinking. Applejack freed passengers trapped in their rooms. Fluttershy turned up with life jackets for the petting-zoo animals. Pinkie went after the chef who’d banned her from the buffet. Rarity and Twilight got the passengers onto a lifeboat of their own making, and Rainbow put her speed to work getting them to shore. In the midst of it all, Sunset helped a frightened little girl find her mother.

The journey through the island is a particularly curious meeting of the two worlds. Sunset knows something about both forms of life, yet she still has friends experiencing the crossing for the first time. Rainbow's observation matters; so does Twilight's caution. When the ship needs them, both contributions can find their place without either girl having to win the argument.

The passengers still needed a way home. Taking them through Equestria meant Princess Twilight wound up with a castle full of unexpected ponies. It was an ambitious solution even by the standards of Canterlot High school trips.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 18 · a game and a voyage

tracks.announcement_text:
The Starswirled Music Festival is coming up. The girls have a great many things to pack, and Sunset has one particular performance in mind.

Applejack and Rarity put together some advice about what to bring to the festival. Applejack had sunscreen, hand sanitizer, toilet paper, and a sleeping bag in mind. Rarity favored a parasol, a privacy screen, and pillows in quantities that raised a practical question about how she expected anybody to carry them. Then she showed Applejack the RV. Both sets of recommendations suddenly made perfect sense. They were going to the same place and sleeping in entirely different sorts of luxury, at least in their heads.

Their friends had a say about what to wear. Rainbow wanted enough room to dance. Applejack stood by boots that had seen some use. Nature supplied Fluttershy with some charming little birds. Rarity rather fancied they had gathered out of an appreciation of fashion. Fluttershy could translate what they wanted, which was a meal of worms brought up specially for them. Twilight recommended ear protection and enough equipment to find your way back. She had even thought about both kinds of compass. There wasn’t the slightest danger of mistaking one girl for another once they had all dressed themselves.

It warms me that Sunset is as pleased to meet a lighting technician as a performer. A concert has many kinds of magic in it, and some of its most essential work is done where the audience never thinks to look. As a radio host, I have a particular appreciation for such invisible labor.

Twilight’s little camera drone went to Starswirled with them. Sunset got a backstage pass and took it along. Given access to the people behind PostCrush, she got tremendously excited about meeting the woman who ran the lights and the man whose work on reverb she recognized. Spending time in a band had given Sunset a whole additional set of people to be starstruck by. It’s lovely to think of what it meant to the crew to have somebody ask for their picture in a room full of performers.

Pinkie borrowed the drone to show people her favorite queues. The wait for nachos gave her ample opportunity to weigh the toppings before choosing all of them. The photo-booth line gave everybody time to practice a pose. She recommended one line without the slightest idea where it led. The bathroom queue, she felt, had all the people it needed to become a conga line. You began to understand why it could take the better part of a morning to get across the festival grounds with her.

Everyone wanted a say about filters when Sunset took a picture of them together. The girls experimented until Pinkie came up with a party picture complete with cake. Sunset liked it. Fluttershy liked the look of the cake. Applejack wanted the name of the filter so she could use it herself. Pinkie had gone ahead and decorated the actual space. The cake looked good for the soundest possible reason.

The act Sunset most wanted to see at the Starswirled Music Festival was PostCrush. Pinkie loved them, too. K-Lo on vocals and guitar, Su-Z on drums, the two of them back together onstage. Sunset had the occasion all laid out in her head. Pinkie could see quite a few things worth stopping for between breakfast and the stage. Where Sunset saw the risk of losing their spot, Pinkie saw a day out with her best friend who, as a bonus, loved the very same band.

Things got sticky around a churro cart. They got thrown out and missed the show. Pinkie tried to apologize. Sunset, bitterly disappointed, made sure Pinkie knew whose fault she thought it was. She went to sleep after missing the evening she’d wanted and woke up with the whole first day of the festival ahead of her again.

To begin with, that was a marvelous piece of luck. Sunset could allow for every delay. When that failed she could simply go without Pinkie. She got a spot right up front. PostCrush came on. The thing she had wanted so badly really happened, and Pinkie had to spend the day knowing that her best friend would happily have it without her. In the morning the day started over. The only person in the group who could remember what Sunset had done with all those chances was Sunset.

She even tried taking Rarity’s RV away from the festival. It broke down. Eventually she wrote to Princess Twilight, who identified the likely cause as an Equestrian artifact called the Time Twirler. Adagio, Aria, and Sonata were at Starswirled, singing a song called “Find the Magic” about one day running into the next. It was an unfortunate choice of title for anybody trying to convince Sunset of their innocence just then. Sunset had reason to ask what they knew. The Dazzlings had lost their magic at Canterlot High and were getting by without it. Adagio could be thoroughly unpleasant and still be telling the truth. Of all people, Sunset might have appreciated how it felt to be the first suspect on the strength of something you’d done a long time ago.

When Sunset put some effort into enjoying the things Pinkie wanted to do, she found she could have a pretty good day along the route she’d been trying to hurry them past. Eventually the two got backstage and met their idols. K-Lo and Su-Z had found the Time Twirler. If anything went wrong during their set, they could take the day over and play it better. Su-Z was tired. K-Lo could still think of things that might go wrong. From out in the crowd Sunset had been envying two musicians who had got themselves into an exaggerated version of her own trouble.

The Time Twirler gives the idea of a perfect day an unusually literal form. Suppose one could change the order of every event until the outcome looked precisely as intended. What might disappear in the process? Sunset eventually makes room for something that none of her earlier plans could have predicted. My lilac mane swishes with quiet delight at the thought that the imperfect day was the one worth keeping.

Getting that day back for everybody involved some difficulty with festival security, a remarkably hard churro, and one guard who remembered that Sunset had treated him decently. Pinkie knocked the Time Twirler free. Sunset smashed it. K-Lo and Su-Z now had to play a show straight through, with whatever mistakes happened along the way. Sunset and Pinkie got to play with them. There was no way either of them could have put that on the itinerary.

In the morning Sunset woke up to the second day. After about three weeks of yesterday, she wanted to spend it with Pinkie. For once they were in the happy position of having no idea exactly how it would go.

And Sunset got to sing at Starswirled herself. Rain came down on the stage and the crowd during “Let It Rain.” A wet audience can be a formidable sight from behind a microphone. Sunset stayed up there singing about weathering a bad stretch while the water fell on her too. By the end the storm was lifting. At the Battle of the Bands, she’d stood at the edge of the Rainbooms’ stage waiting for a sign that she belonged at a microphone. Here were people prepared to stand out in the rain to hear her.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 19 · a day at starswirled

tracks.announcement_text:
Let us linger at Starswirled a little longer. Each of the girls has her own favorite way to spend a festival day.

At Starswirled, the day you had depended a great deal on which girl you followed out of the tent. Take Sunset, still asleep after the all-night drum circle. In her sleep she was asking Princess Celestia for five more minutes before magic school. There were at least three good friends within earshot, each with a different idea of a good morning.

Go with Applejack and you could get to know the girl who set the campsite up every morning while everybody else slept. She’d even been rolling the sushi in the mini fridge. There were pancakes in Sunset’s immediate future, once she helped build the fire pit. Rainbow, meanwhile, had a series of yoga poses that got increasingly difficult to sustain on very little sleep. You had to stick with her long enough to see where she’d put you when the sun came up. That view was why she’d woken Sunset. As for Pinkie, she knew a breakfast involving waffles, cupcakes, sprinkles, and jelly beans. Sunset could have five gloriously energetic minutes with her and then a stomachache. When the sugar wore off, the drummer who’d helped keep the campsite awake all night was asleep herself.

Over at DJ Pon-3’s stage, the last drop of the beat was up for grabs. Take Sunset up with the DJ and the controls became an eight-bit game she could play, the little electronic sounds coming out over the crowd. Give Fluttershy the spot and she needed a minute. A festival stage is a long way from singing to the animals at the shelter. A few animals in attendance helped her find the beat, though, and by the time she let out a wolf howl there was very little doubt who’d made that sound. Or the DJ could hand a banjo to Applejack’s brother Big Mac. He had a way of making himself understood in very few words, and here he could dispense with the words altogether. It turns out a banjo will go quite nicely with a dance beat if the people in charge of both are willing to try.

Rarity had chosen suede and fringe for the festival. The rain took an interest almost as soon as she’d set foot outside. Applejack could find something good about a patch of fresh mud. She was thinking of fishing bait. Rarity, following the same sound principle, could see the makings of a mud mask. Twilight had thought up all kinds of protection against bad weather, although the materials immediately available to her were garbage bags. Rarity could make those into rain ponchos. Or she could call Vignette Valencia, of all people. Vignette took one look at Rarity’s wet hair and liked what the rain had done to it. With her encouragement, having your hair drenched at Starswirled could become the look everyone else was trying to get. It’s rather nice to think that, after all that trouble at Equestria Land, Rarity could still call Vignette with an extremely urgent question about her hair.

The mud also produced a small, bedraggled dog near the food trucks. Who got her back to her person depended largely on whom the dog took a fancy to. She could follow Rarity, who was perfectly willing to be friendly at a little distance and had considerable difficulty communicating the part about the distance. Retreating from a muddy puppy took Rarity all the way into the lounge where Su-Z of PostCrush recognized her dog. The puppy’s name was Princess Thunder Guts. Rarity’s reward for delivering her was a feather boa. If the princess picked Spike, the two dogs could fit a fair amount of eating and playing into the afternoon before their goodbye. Spike took it hard until she gave him a lick on the cheek. Fluttershy could shorten the entire operation considerably by asking the puppy who she belonged to. Su-Z got her dog back promptly that way, although Spike might reasonably have preferred the longer route.

All these festival afternoons remind me that a place has as many possible experiences as it has companions. One friend knows where to find the sunrise; another knows how to make a muddy morning into an occasion. Twilight's itinerary could be excellent on its own terms and still leave out a death metal show with Fluttershy. I am quite charmed by that particular discovery.

Applejack, who had been up early enough to make everybody else’s morning possible, wanted a good place at Dirk Thistleweed’s concert. She got right down in front, where somebody stomped on her foot. Rainbow and Pinkie helped her out of the crush. Applejack urged them to get back to the stage. She knew what they would be missing. They knew what she would be missing, too.

With Rainbow for company, Applejack could try a preparation Rainbow knew from her coach. The smell of it drew Dirk himself, seeking relief for a hoarse throat. Suddenly the girl who’d given up her spot in front had her favorite performer singing within arm’s reach. If Pinkie took charge, there was a wheelbarrow, a hill with a view, and finally Pinkie onstage personally nudging Dirk into Applejack’s line of sight. Or Applejack could notice Snips off by himself. He thought Snails had left him. She offered to keep him company. When Snails turned up with Dirk and an invitation to watch from the side of the stage, Applejack was there to share it. Sitting out a favorite song is considerably easier when you get some say in whom you sit beside.

Twilight had written an algorithm to fit the best possible route between bands into the available time. Her electronic planner couldn’t survive the quantity of sweat Bulk Biceps introduced into the equation. Spike and Twilight were obliged to see what somebody else thought worth hearing. There was Principal Celestia, spending the day with her sister Luna and Cranky Doodle. The three of them had been coming since the festival started. Twilight was so surprised to learn that her principal did things outside school that she practically said it to her face. Celestia could show her around, and by evening she was teasing Twilight about sending her a letter after every festival to tell her what she’d learned.

Following Micro Chips would turn up an equally good surprise. He had a second life onstage as MC Dex Effex. And following Fluttershy would mean going to hear Skull Cruncher, a death metal band. Fluttershy was a little nervous about what her friend would think of the music she loved. Twilight was willing to give it a go with her. Of all the musical discoveries that might have made it onto a meticulously planned agenda, how high do you suppose Twilight had ranked seeing a death metal show with Fluttershy?
tracks.title: through the mirror · 20 · the festival from many sides

tracks.announcement_text:
The girls have come home from the festival. Winter is approaching, and there are a few more memories I would like to share with you, friend.

The robot from the pet show gave everybody ample opportunity to notice the girls at work. Competing for a ribbon, JVJ-24601 had been manageable. When a much bigger, out-of-control JVJ came crashing into a concert at school, even its builder’s remote could do nothing with it. The girls got him out of harm’s way. The machine blasted them clear through the wall and onto the playing field, where Sunset discovered that her geode had fallen off. Once it was back in her hands the seven could bring the machine down together. There had been some doubt at the pet show over whether a robot qualified as a pet. From a school maintenance point of view, there was now a very good argument for entering a dog.

Pinkie Pie was a frozen yogurt shop’s thousandth customer. Her prize was one free topping. They might as well have asked her to pick a favorite sprinkle. Applejack liked fruit. Pinkie liked candy. Hand the decision to those two and Pinkie could choose candied cherries in the cheerful belief that she’d found a loophole, while Applejack quietly swapped them for fresh ones. Both girls would go home pleased with their cleverness. Ask Twilight and she could work out that chocolate-covered walnuts went beautifully with the flavors Pinkie had chosen. Unfortunately frozen yogurt keeps its own time while you’re doing the sums. Pinkie was perfectly happy to drink it melted. Fluttershy had explicitly asked to sit this decision out. She was animal-sitting, and the shop had rules. Open the door to consult her anyway and all the animals could come streaming in, the shop could get shut down, and a squirrel could supply the final sprinkle of acorn. That's quite a lot of excitement to get for free.

The frozen yogurt shop presents a surprisingly extravagant set of possible universes for one free topping. Some decisions really can be left to the pony or girl eating the dessert, friend. And perhaps Fluttershy's request to stay with the animals was already all the guidance her friends needed.

Another afternoon found Fluttershy, Applejack, and Rarity at Sunset’s place when they all got invited to Bulk’s costume party. Fluttershy knew she wanted to go. What she couldn’t picture was what she’d wear. Sunset had some truly alarming things in her closet and could turn a soft-spoken friend into a tentacled creature convincing enough to terrify their host. Rarity could spend ages putting together an exquisite princess dress, reveal at the last moment that she meant to wear it herself, then offer Fluttershy her pick of the dresses she already owned. Or Applejack could dig out a two-person pony costume. With Fluttershy at the front and Applejack bringing up the rear, neither would have to make the entrance alone. Of all the ways those girls had ever come into a room as a pony, this one definitely took the most coordination.

Winter at Canterlot High brought the usual collection of urgent seasonal business. Pinkie had seven minutes to deliver a soufflé to Rarity. Applejack’s family anticipated an attempt on their cider. Somebody had left the key to the toy donations at school. Any one of these could keep the seven girls quite as busy as a magical emergency.

There was also the morning they tried to manufacture a snow day after an unsuccessful night of studying. Pinkie built a snowman out of potatoes. Rarity knitted it a scarf. Sunset contributed a painted winter view, which was a considerable application of her artistic talents to the problem of an upcoming test. They got caught. By then they’d done an impressive amount of practical study on the subject of water vapor, which Rainbow had known they might need.

Take the soufflé. Pinkie baked one for Rarity every year, and every year it sank before she could get it to her. If you’ve ever watched somebody eat a thing you made especially for them, you know the little moment she kept missing. This year she’d worked out the timing. The obstacle she hadn’t factored in was a snowball fight in the front yard of such dimensions that getting a dessert across it required help from Sunset. With the minutes running down, Rarity came to Pinkie. She got to taste it in time. Pinkie finally got to see her do it.

At the Apples’, Twilight entered into the spirit of the cider-making party with a game-theory matrix. Flim and Flam had made something of a tradition of swindling the family, and this year she and the Apples were ready for them. A jug of salt-and-pepper water, an elaborate set of predictions about who would outsmart whom, and Granny Smith’s considerable enthusiasm for getting one over on the pair all came into play. It’s hard to imagine a nicer development for the girl from Crystal Prep than being asked to a family party where bringing a game-theory matrix made her an especially welcome guest.

For the toy drive the girls had a wagon and donations, and the donations were safely locked away. Sunset’s key was in her locker at school. The school was closed. Soon the proposals for getting in involved air vents, a cupcake diversion, and Applejack lifting the building. Twilight phoned Principal Celestia and asked if she’d open the door. The children got their toys. Later Twilight realized she’d left something else back at school, at which point the attractions of a well-planned heist appeared to be growing on her.

At the mall, Rainbow realized she’d forgotten to get Fluttershy a present for their exchange. She scrambled to find something that would suit her and came up with an instant camera. Fluttershy’s old camera had broken. It turned out she already had a replacement. Fluttershy already knew what she would do with two. She’d be able to take candid pictures of bear cubs from different angles. Of all the elaborate saves Rainbow had pulled off that year, this one came down to having a friend with unusually specific plans for photographing bears.

The photograph Applejack wanted was a little more formal. Her family had a tradition of taking a themed picture for the holidays, and she wanted one with these girls. She explained the cornucopia she had in mind. Rarity offered to see to the wardrobe. This was the moment somebody might have asked Applejack exactly what she meant by a cornucopia. Instead Rarity got to work.

Six girls dressed as produce had exactly until the bell to reach the auditorium unseen. They were still in the hall when it rang. There are things you do for a friend which you might prefer the rest of the student body never found out about.

My silver sigil glimmers with quiet affection. That holiday photograph is not the one Applejack initially imagined, yet it contains something the original plan could never have anticipated: a story all seven girls can tell. Perhaps the nicest thing about a shared memory is that it can have more than one voice and still belong to everyone.

Applejack was waiting in her regular clothes. She’d meant the cornucopia as a backdrop. By the time she’d finished laughing, her friends had a fairly clear idea of what she ought to wear, too.

Photo Finish took the picture. Applejack got her holiday card for the whole school, with all seven of them in it. If you wanted to know how they’d ended up dressed that way, you’d have to ask Rarity what she’d understood, Applejack what she’d actually said, and the other five about the walk down the hall. Pull up a chair for that part. Everybody remembers it a little differently.

And here we shall leave the girls for a little while, with the picture taken and the stories still theirs to share. Thank you for keeping me company, friend.
tracks.title: through the mirror · 21 · a picture to send home

A throne built upon fear may command obedience, but it cannot command friendship. Let the strength of a ruler be measured by those who are safe beneath that rule.

As above, so below.

My silver sigil of the fourth dimension is with you.

So mote it be, and so it is.

Amen.

So mote it be, and so it is.

Amen.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 27:3 · the together trees · wisdom

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The elder age, chapter one, historical account one.

According to the ancient history remembered by Tirek, the land that would become Equestria consisted of farms and pastures before Grogar proclaimed himself emperor. Grogar was remembered as the Father of Monsters and credited with creating terrible beasts. The later figure who claimed to be Grogar was Discord in disguise.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 1:1 · the first remembered empire · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The elder age, chapter one, historical account two.

According to the account later told by the false Grogar, the unicorn Gusty the Great opposed the ancient ruler by taking his Bewitching Bell and hiding it in an enchanted cave on Mount Everhoof. The bell could take, contain and release magic. The ultimate fate of Grogar is not recorded.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 1:2 · gusty the great · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The elder age, chapter one, historical account three.

No surviving account establishes the creation of the world, the first appearance of ponykind, or the origin of magic itself. The ancient reign of Grogar is one of the earliest remembered events, not an account of creation.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 1:3 · the beginnings of the world · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The three tribes, chapter two, historical account one.

In the Hearth’s Warming story, earth ponies cultivated the land and provided food for the other tribes. Their strength and agricultural abilities were indispensable to the survival of ponykind. Chancellor Puddinghead and Smart Cookie are remembered among their leaders and representatives at the founding.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 2:1 · the earth ponies · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The three tribes, chapter two, historical account two.

In the Hearth’s Warming story, the pegasi governed the weather and supplied the conditions necessary for growing crops. Commander Hurricane and Private Pansy represented their tribe in the search for a new homeland.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 2:2 · the pegasi · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The three tribes, chapter two, historical account three.

In the Hearth’s Warming story, the unicorns practiced horn-borne magic and bore responsibility for the movement of the sun and moon. Princess Platinum and Clover the Clever represented their tribe. The three peoples depended upon one another even when their rulers were divided by distrust.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 2:3 · the unicorns · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The founding of Equestria, chapter three, historical account one.

According to the Hearth’s Warming account, as the three tribes quarreled, the Windigos were drawn to their hatred. The cold increased, food grew scarce, and each tribe blamed the others. Their search for new lands brought them together again, but their leaders could not agree upon its possession.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 3:1 · the winter of discord · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The founding of Equestria, chapter three, historical account two.

In the Hearth’s Warming story, Clover the Clever, Smart Cookie and Private Pansy recognized their common plight and became friends. Their friendship kindled a magical fire that drove back the Windigos. They kept it alive through the night with stories, laughter and song until its warmth thawed their leaders and helped reconcile them.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 3:2 · the fire in the cave · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The founding of Equestria, chapter three, historical account three.

According to the Hearth’s Warming story, the three tribes reconciled and established Equestria as a common homeland. The founding is remembered at Hearth’s Warming, when the peoples recall the overcoming of their ancient division through friendship.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 3:3 · one homeland · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Pillars of Old Equestria, chapter four, historical account one.

Star Swirl the Bearded embodied sorcery; Rockhoof, strength; Mistmane, beauty; Flash Magnus, bravery; Somnambula, hope; and Mage Meadowbrook, healing. Their individual deeds became the subjects of ancient legends.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 4:1 · the six pillars · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Pillars of Old Equestria, chapter four, historical account two.

Stygian gathered the six protectors together. Seeking their respect and a place beside them in battle, he took their artifacts to Ponhenge intending to make copies. They believed he wanted their power and cast him out.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 4:2 · stygian · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Pillars of Old Equestria, chapter four, historical account three.

In his isolation Stygian encountered a mysterious darkness and became the Pony of Shadows. The Pillars banished him to Limbo, sacrificing themselves in the process. When the Pillars were brought back, the darkness returned with them. Starlight Glimmer urged the others to seek reconciliation rather than simply banish their foe. Stygian was separated from the darkness, which was sent back to Limbo, and the Pillars recognized their misunderstanding.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 4:3 · the pony of shadows · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Tree of Harmony, chapter five, historical account one.

Before their disappearance, the Pillars left a seed imbued with their magic and virtues to protect Equestria. It grew into the crystalline Tree of Harmony in the Everfree Forest.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 5:1 · the seed · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Tree of Harmony, chapter five, historical account two.

The Tree bore the Elements of Harmony, which the royal sisters discovered and used in defense of Equestria. The Tree’s own magic helped contain the growth of the Everfree Forest. It also held back the plunderseeds Discord had planted before his petrification; when the Tree weakened, the vines grew until the Elements were returned.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 5:2 · the six elements · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Tree of Harmony, chapter five, historical account three.

The Tree communicated in visions and tested the bonds between creatures. Even after Sombra destroyed its original form, its power endured and a new crystalline treehouse arose. Its ultimate nature and the origin of its awareness remain unknown.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 5:3 · the living tree · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The royal sisters and the heavens, chapter six, historical account one.

Opaline’s account of Skyros, the alicorn homeland, places Celestia and Luna there in their youth. The location and later history of Skyros are not known.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 6:1 · the alicorn homeland · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The royal sisters and the heavens, chapter six, historical account two.

According to Twilight’s commemorative play, before Celestia took responsibility for the sun, raising it required Star Swirl and five other great sorcerers. The effort permanently depleted the magic of the unicorns assisting him. Celestia discovered that she could raise the sun without losing her magic. The 1,111th anniversary of her first sunrise was celebrated during Twilight’s time.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 6:2 · the rising sun · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The royal sisters and the heavens, chapter six, historical account three.

Luna bore responsibility for the moon and the night. The sisters ruled together, and their old castle stood in the Everfree Forest. After Luna’s banishment, Celestia maintained both celestial duties until her sister returned.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 6:3 · the rising moon · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Discord and the age of chaos, chapter seven, historical account one.

Discord ruled the land through chaos, transforming its landscape and overturning ordinary physical laws. Celestia and Luna used the Elements of Harmony to turn him to stone.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 7:1 · the reign of chaos · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Discord and the age of chaos, chapter seven, historical account two.

Discord can change matter, gravity, weather and space. He also inhabits a realm of his own. His continued existence depends upon his chaotic nature; when he denied it entirely, he began to disappear.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 7:2 · the nature of discord · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Discord and the age of chaos, chapter seven, historical account three.

Through friendship Discord learned to care for others without ceasing to be the spirit of chaos. His powers are formidable but not unlimited: certain artifacts and magical substances can suppress or remove them.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 7:3 · friendship and chaos · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Crystal Empire, chapter eight, historical account one.

The Crystal Heart protects the Crystal Empire from the cold and channels the light and love of its inhabitants. The crystal ponies renew this protection through their communal celebration.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 8:1 · the crystal heart · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Crystal Empire, chapter eight, historical account two.

King Sombra seized the empire and enslaved its inhabitants. Celestia and Luna defeated him and banished him into the frozen north. His curse caused the empire to disappear for a thousand years.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 8:2 · the rule of sombra · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Crystal Empire, chapter eight, historical account three.

When the empire returned, its people were still present, though they struggled to remember their past. The Crystal Fair helped revive their memories and traditions. Sombra sought to reclaim it, but the Crystal Heart was restored to its place and the empire was freed. Cadance and Shining Armor became its protectors.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 8:3 · the restoration · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Nightmare Moon and the millennium, chapter nine, historical account one.

Luna grew bitter because the ponies delighted in the day but slept through the night. As Nightmare Moon, she refused to lower the moon and sought to bring everlasting night.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 9:1 · the rebellion of the night · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Nightmare Moon and the millennium, chapter nine, historical account two.

Celestia, unable to reach her sister, used the Elements of Harmony to banish Nightmare Moon to the moon. For a thousand years Celestia ruled alone and bore responsibility for both day and night.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 9:2 · the thousand years · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Nightmare Moon and the millennium, chapter nine, historical account three.

When the thousand years had passed, Nightmare Moon returned. Twilight Sparkle and her five companions wielded the Elements of Harmony, freeing Luna from her dark transformation. The sisters were reconciled and resumed their shared responsibilities.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 9:3 · the return of luna · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The six Elements of Harmony, chapter ten, historical account one.

Honesty, kindness, laughter, generosity and loyalty are the five Elements first recognized by Twilight and her companions. Their bearers were Applejack, Fluttershy, Pinkie Pie, Rarity and Rainbow Dash, respectively.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 10:1 · the five known virtues · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The six Elements of Harmony, chapter ten, historical account two.

Twilight discovered that the sixth Element, magic, was awakened through her recognition of the friendship joining them. Its appearance completed the sixfold union.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 10:2 · the sixth element · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The six Elements of Harmony, chapter ten, historical account three.

The Elements can purify, restore, banish or petrify. Their bearers eventually returned the jewels to the Tree. Friendship continued to have power even when the physical Elements were no longer available, and creatures beyond the original six could share in that power.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 10:3 · beyond the artifacts · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The nature of ponykind, chapter eleven, historical account one.

Earth ponies possess characteristic strength and an affinity for growing things. Pegasi fly and manipulate clouds and weather. Unicorns perform spells through their horns. Each people has innate magic, though its expression differs.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 11:1 · earth, wings and horn · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The nature of ponykind, chapter eleven, historical account two.

Crystal ponies possess a distinctive magical crystalline appearance, associated with the Crystal Empire and its Heart. Aquatic forms are also known; transformation magic can grant forms suited to life beneath the water.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 11:2 · crystal and aquatic ponies · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The nature of ponykind, chapter eleven, historical account three.

When Tirek drained pony magic, even pegasi whose wings remained intact lost the ability to fly. Earth ponies lost their strength and unicorns lost their spells. The gifts of ponykind depend on more than physical form.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 11:3 · magic and the body · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The alicorns, chapter twelve, historical account one.

Celestia is associated with the sun; Luna with the moon and dreams; Cadance with love; Twilight with friendship and magic. Their abilities differ, and their rank does not establish unlimited power.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 12:1 · the royal alicorns · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The alicorns, chapter twelve, historical account two.

Twilight helped her friends restore their rightful cutie marks, completed an unfinished spell by Star Swirl the Bearded, and attained alicornhood. Later she became Princess of Friendship and succeeded the royal sisters.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 12:2 · the ascension of twilight · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The alicorns, chapter twelve, historical account three.

Flurry Heart was born an alicorn, an event unprecedented in the memory of the royal sisters within Equestria. In a later age Sunny Starscout manifested magical wings and a horn. Alicorns can live for exceptionally long periods, but no account establishes that all are immortal.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 12:3 · birth and transformation · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Cutie marks and destiny, chapter thirteen, historical account one.

A pony’s cutie mark appears as the pony discovers a defining talent or aspect of the self. The marks of the six friends arose through events connected by Rainbow Dash’s first sonic rainboom.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 13:1 · the discovery of a gift · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Cutie marks and destiny, chapter thirteen, historical account two.

Magic can exchange cutie marks, alter their appearance or remove them. Starlight Glimmer’s settlement demonstrates the harm of enforcing sameness through the suppression of individual abilities.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 13:2 · the exchange and removal of marks · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Cutie marks and destiny, chapter thirteen, historical account three.

When Celestia and Luna exchanged marks, they also exchanged the abilities associated with their duties. The Cutie Map summons particular bearers in response to problems of friendship. The ultimate origin of marks and their relationship to destiny remain unresolved.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 13:3 · identity and vocation · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The workings of magic, chapter fourteen, historical account one.

Magical power can be taken from living creatures, accumulated and returned. Tirek feeds upon stolen magic. The alicorn princesses entrusted their own power to Twilight in an attempt to keep it from him.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 14:1 · the taking and giving of power · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The workings of magic, chapter fourteen, historical account two.

The Bewitching Bell stores and releases magic; the Alicorn Amulet grants great power but corrupts its wearer; the throne of Chrysalis suppresses magic other than changeling magic. Different artifacts affect power in different ways.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 14:2 · enchanted vessels · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The workings of magic, chapter fourteen, historical account three.

Twilight’s later message teaches that magic can evolve and grow stronger. After the three tribes reunited and magic returned, a later surge of magic awakened new plant-growing abilities among earth ponies. The known workings of magic are not confined to those of the ancient kingdom.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 14:3 · the growth of magic · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Love, hatred and the heart, chapter fifteen, historical account one.

Changelings traditionally fed upon love. Thorax and those who followed his example learned to give love freely, underwent a physical transformation and no longer needed to steal love to satisfy their hunger. Love also empowers the protection of the Crystal Empire.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 15:1 · the sustenance of love · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Love, hatred and the heart, chapter fifteen, historical account two.

Windigos are strengthened by hatred and strife and bring cold in their wake. The Fire of Friendship overcame them at the founding of Equestria, and their return in the later struggle showed that the ancient danger had not vanished.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 15:2 · the hunger of winter spirits · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Love, hatred and the heart, chapter fifteen, historical account three.

Kirin become fiery Niriks in anger. Their community once entered the Stream of Silence to cool their emotions and give up speech, but eventually recovered their voices and learned that disagreement need not destroy friendship.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 15:3 · the fire of anger · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Dreams and the realms beyond, chapter sixteen, historical account one.

Luna enters the dreams of sleeping creatures, offers counsel and can bring many sleepers into a shared dream. Luna created the Tantabus to give herself nightmares as punishment for her deeds as Nightmare Moon. Her guilt strengthened it, and it threatened to enter the waking world. When Luna forgave herself, the danger ended.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 16:1 · the realm of dreams · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Dreams and the realms beyond, chapter sixteen, historical account two.

Limbo is a place between worlds in which time does not pass normally. The Pillars and Stygian remained there for more than a thousand years without ordinary aging.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 16:2 · limbo · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Dreams and the realms beyond, chapter sixteen, historical account three.

Tartarus is a prison guarded by Cerberus and accessible through physical gates. Tirek and dangerous beasts were imprisoned there. No account establishes it as the universal destination of the dead. Discord’s own realm obeys very different physical laws.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 16:3 · tartarus and the chaos realm · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The mirror and the paths of time, chapter seventeen, historical account one.

The Crystal Mirror leads to a world inhabited by humans. A traveler’s body can change to suit the other world. Many inhabitants have recognizable counterparts on either side. The mirror’s original thirty-moon opening cycle was later modified.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 17:1 · the mirror between worlds · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The mirror and the paths of time, chapter seventeen, historical account two.

Star Swirl devised spells capable of carrying a pony into the past. Starlight Glimmer altered one such spell to interfere with the event that joined the destinies of Twilight and her friends.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 17:2 · the spells of time · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The mirror and the paths of time, chapter seventeen, historical account three.

The altered histories revealed a kingdom at war with Sombra, changeling conquest, eternal night, Discord’s unchecked rule, industrial devastation and a desolate wasteland. The original history was restored. Whether those other histories continue independently is unknown.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 17:3 · the roads not taken · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Canterlot and the heartlands, chapter eighteen, historical account one.

The royal capital houses the court, magical education and important records. Celestia established her school for gifted unicorns, and Twilight received her education and mentorship there.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 18:1 · canterlot · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Canterlot and the heartlands, chapter eighteen, historical account two.

Ponyville grew from an agricultural settlement into a center of friendship and interspecies education. Cloudsdale is a cloud-borne pegasus city with facilities for making weather. Manehattan is a large urban center; Appleloosa is a frontier agricultural settlement.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 18:2 · ponyville and cloudsdale · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Canterlot and the heartlands, chapter eighteen, historical account three.

The Everfree Forest is unusual to the ponies because its weather, plants and animals act without their customary supervision. The Castle of the Two Sisters and the ancient Tree of Harmony stood within this forest.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 18:3 · the everfree forest · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Dragon Lands, chapter nineteen, historical account one.

Dragons possess fire, strength and magic of their own. Spike can send written messages through his fire breath. Dragon growth can also be influenced by greed, as demonstrated by Spike’s rapid transformation and return to his former size.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 19:1 · the dragons · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Dragon Lands, chapter nineteen, historical account two.

The Dragon Lord holds the Bloodstone Scepter, which can summon dragons. Ember became Dragon Lord after the Gauntlet of Fire and began to foster friendship with the ponies.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 19:2 · the bloodstone scepter · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The Dragon Lands, chapter nineteen, historical account three.

In the age after Twilight, the dragons were found in magical slumber on the Isle of Scaly. The Dragonstone preserves dragon magic. Opaline sought to take the power of dragon fire for herself.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 19:3 · the dragons in the later age · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Griffonstone and the northern peoples, chapter twenty, historical account one.

According to Griffonstone’s traditional account, King Grover united the griffons through the Idol of Boreas. During King Guto’s reign the monster Arimaspi stole it, and the treasure was lost. The loss became associated with the decline of Griffonstone’s unity and prosperity.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 20:1 · the idol of boreas · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Griffonstone and the northern peoples, chapter twenty, historical account two.

The history of Griffonstone shows how attachment to a treasure can fail to sustain a people after its loss. New friendships helped griffons rediscover bonds of community without recovering the ancient idol.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 20:2 · the restoration of friendship · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Griffonstone and the northern peoples, chapter twenty, historical account three.

Yakyakistan is a mountainous homeland of the yaks, a people with strong traditions and a distinct political identity. Their friendship with Equestria developed through mutual respect rather than the abandonment of their customs.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 20:3 · yakyakistan · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The changeling kingdom, chapter twenty-one, historical account one.

The changelings once served Queen Chrysalis. Their shapeshifting powers allowed them to impersonate others and steal love. Chrysalis’s throne protected the hive by suppressing foreign magic.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 21:1 · the old hive · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The changeling kingdom, chapter twenty-one, historical account two.

Thorax discovered that changelings could share love. When the others followed his example, they transformed and ceased to depend on the theft of love. Chrysalis rejected their new way and departed.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 21:2 · the giving of love · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The changeling kingdom, chapter twenty-one, historical account three.

Under Thorax, the changelings developed a different society and established relations with other kingdoms. Their transformation demonstrates that a people need not remain bound to its former habits or ruler.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 21:3 · a renewed people · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The sea, the mountains and the distant lands, chapter twenty-two, historical account one.

The hippogriffs once dwelt on Mount Aris. When the Storm King threatened them, Queen Novo used a magical pearl to transform her people into sea ponies, establishing their refuge beneath the waves.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 22:1 · mount aris and seaquestria · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The sea, the mountains and the distant lands, chapter twenty-two, historical account two.

After the Storm King’s defeat, the hippogriffs could return to Mount Aris. Their transformative magic allowed families to live both above and beneath the sea. Neither home required them to abandon their shared identity.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 22:2 · the return to the mountain · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The sea, the mountains and the distant lands, chapter twenty-two, historical account three.

The kirin inhabit a grove governed by their own customs. Beyond Equestria are other peoples and settlements, including the diverse trading town of Klugetown. Abyssinia is also known among the lands of the wider world.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 22:3 · the kirin grove and distant settlements · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The creatures of shadow and strife, chapter twenty-three, historical account one.

Tirek and his brother Scorpan came from a distant land seeking pony magic. Scorpan befriended the ponies and warned the royal sisters. Tirek was captured and imprisoned in Tartarus, but later escaped and again sought to absorb the magic of Equestria.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 23:1 · tirek and scorpan · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The creatures of shadow and strife, chapter twenty-three, historical account two.

Adagio Dazzle, Aria Blaze and Sonata Dusk used their songs to turn listeners against one another and feed upon the resulting discord. Star Swirl banished them from Equestria into the human world.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 23:2 · the sirens · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The creatures of shadow and strife, chapter twenty-three, historical account three.

Sombra wielded fear, shadow and domination. The darkness that joined itself to Stygian had a different and still unknown origin. Other dangerous beings include the Windigos and the Tantabus; their powers arise through different forms of magical influence.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 23:3 · the shadows · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The succession of Twilight, chapter twenty-four, historical account one.

Twilight’s work extended beyond the defense of the kingdom. Her castle and its Cutie Map guided the bearers of the Elements toward places where friendship was in need of repair.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 24:1 · the princess of friendship · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The succession of Twilight, chapter twenty-four, historical account two.

The school brought together ponies and students from other peoples, including changelings, dragons, griffons, yaks and hippogriffs. It formally extended the teaching of friendship across the boundaries of species and kingdoms.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 24:2 · the school of friendship · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The succession of Twilight, chapter twenty-four, historical account three.

Celestia and Luna retired, and Twilight succeeded them as ruler of Equestria. Her first royal decree established the Council of Friendship, whose members agreed to meet once a moon. In the years that followed, they kept their friendships alive and continued to govern and protect Equestria together.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 24:3 · the council and the throne · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Opaline and the preservation of magic, chapter twenty-five, historical account one.

Opaline Arcana was banished from Skyros and remembered Celestia and Luna from their youth. She sought to rule ponykind and regarded ordinary ponies as beneath alicorns. According to Spike’s later account, she attacked dragons to become a Fire Alicorn.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 25:1 · the fire alicorn · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Opaline and the preservation of magic, chapter twenty-five, historical account two.

In response to the danger, Twilight sealed pony magic within the Unity Crystals. A protective enchantment kept Equestria hidden from Opaline. Dragon magic was also preserved in the Dragonstone, and dragons entered a long magical slumber.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 25:2 · the protective crystals · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. Opaline and the preservation of magic, chapter twenty-five, historical account three.

By the later age, the three tribes had become divided and no longer had access to their former magic. The precise relationship between the preservation of magic, the division of the tribes and the fates of Twilight and the other princesses is not fully recorded. The former capital and institutions no longer occupy their old place in pony society.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 25:3 · the breaking of the old kingdom · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The lost years and the three new homelands, chapter twenty-six, historical account one.

Earth ponies lived in Maretime Bay, where fear of the other tribes had become common. Argyle Starshine preserved accounts of the ancient friendship of ponykind and passed them on to his daughter Sunny.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 26:1 · maretime bay · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The lost years and the three new homelands, chapter twenty-six, historical account two.

Unicorns inhabited Bridlewood and lived without their former spellcasting. Pegasi dwelt in Zephyr Heights and could no longer fly. Their societies retained distinct customs and developed new technologies.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 26:2 · bridlewood and zephyr heights · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The lost years and the three new homelands, chapter twenty-six, historical account three.

The ancient unity of the tribes survived in stories, artifacts and the knowledge of a few ponies. The precise length of the lost years, and the fates of many older kingdoms and peoples, remain unknown.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 26:3 · the forgotten inheritance · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The restoration of unity, chapter twenty-seven, historical account one.

Sunny Starscout and her friends brought the separated tribes together. The crystals united when the ponies themselves chose friendship, restoring magic and enabling the peoples to share a common future.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 27:1 · the unity crystals · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The restoration of unity, chapter twenty-seven, historical account two.

Pegasi recovered flight and unicorns recovered spells. Earth ponies discovered new plant-growing magic. Sunny manifested an alicorn form through magic. Twilight’s preserved message explains that magic changes and can grow stronger.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 27:2 · the new gifts · history

tracks.announcement_text:
From the Chronicles of Harmony. The restoration of unity, chapter twenty-seven, historical account three.

The later age revealed Together Trees linked by their roots and nourished by the unity of ponies. Opaline exploited the network to steal cutie-mark magic. Ponies gathered in friendship at the trees, while Sparky freed Spike from Opaline’s spell. Their combined efforts defeated her and restored the stolen magic.
tracks.title: the chronicles of harmony · 27:3 · the together trees · history
