tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a look at how Rarity dressed for personality.

Rarity had a remarkable talent for giving each pony’s personality another form in cloth. Twilight Sparkle’s first Grand Galloping Gala gown had royal-blue fabric, an icy-blue shoulder drape, and white and cyan stars gathered near the hem. the great star at the throat brought the eye back to Twilight’s face. in Fluttershy’s green gown, the fabric overlapped in curling, leaf-like shapes, with a cyan butterfly at the chest.

what interests me is that the stars and leaves were more than ornaments. their arrangement and the shape of the cloth itself suggested the personalities of the ponies who wore them. to me, that is one of the great pleasures of being a designer: discovering a new language for something one already loves.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · dressing for personality

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a rather unexpected violet curl for Steven Magnet.

Steven Magnet had lost half his moustache, and Rarity replaced it with a long violet lock cut from her own tail. the curling tip preserved the expressive shape of a moustache even though the new hair contrasted with the original.

i rather adore the way the violet curl became a little signature of its own. matching the original color wasn't essential to restoring the shape. a touch of generosity made the difference between an unfortunate mishap and a wonderfully distinctive look.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · a violet curl for Steven Magnet

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Twilight Sparkle’s first Grand Galloping Gala gown.

for the Grand Galloping Gala, Rarity gave Twilight Sparkle a rich royal-blue skirt rounded over the hindquarters. paler icy-blue fabric draped over the shoulders and around the edge. five-pointed stars in white, cyan and deeper blue clustered near the hem, with smaller stars along the shoulder covering. one large pale star sat at the throat. a little star adorned the mane, and the light-blue shoes carried stars of their own. her horn was left free.

Rarity was designing for Twilight's personality. what particularly delights me is the difference in scale: the large star drew the eye toward her face, and the little ones made a lovely rhythm along the skirt. the sky became an arrangement of ornament rather than an astronomical diagram.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Twilight Sparkle's original Gala gown

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Applejack’s orchard-like Gala gown.

Rarity's first Gala dress for Applejack had warm caramel and orange-brown skirt panels beneath hanging green drapes, with golden-yellow fringe along the bottom. red and white bands supplied little flashes of contrast. at the breast was a red apple-shaped clasp with hanging ribbon-like details. a tan Western hat carried red apples and curled markings, and the green hoof coverings repeated those red and white accents. her mane was braided.

i find the palette especially endearing. the greens and warm browns suggested an orchard, while the fringe and hat brought a familiar country vocabulary into formalwear. the result was a dress made to celebrate Applejack, rather than a dress made to turn her into somepony else.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Applejack's original Gala gown

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Pinkie Pie’s rather delightful confection of a Gala dress.

for Pinkie Pie’s Grand Galloping Gala gown, Rarity gave her a rounded raspberry-pink skirt, a short blue-and-white vertically striped bodice, a broad white collar and a pink bow at the breast. orange, yellow and white candy-corn triangles alternated with spiral lollipops along the white scalloped border. lower down, blue loops hung in little swags between pink flowers with white centers. a tiny striped cap, a pink flower and pink shoes with pale-blue bows completed the ensemble.

Pinkie's cheerful personality was the inspiration for the gift. to my eye, the clever thing was how the sweets were organized. the motifs repeated along particular borders instead of being scattered everywhere. what a delightful way to make an exuberant design feel composed.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Pinkie Pie's original Gala gown

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rainbow Dash’s sweeping rainbow Gala gown.

for Rainbow Dash's first Gala gown, Rarity left her blue chest visible and gave her a fine blue necklace with little white bead-like dots and a hanging purple ornament with three lobes. long rainbow stripes flowed rearward, edged with white cloud-like scallops beside the wings and along the side. gold laurel-like ornaments sat in her mane, and golden crisscross straps dressed her hoovsies. her wings remained free.

Rarity drew on Dash's individuality, and i find this one particularly interesting in motion. the broad stripes suggested the speed of a rainboom without needing to reproduce one as a picture. the gold at the head and feet gave the sweeping fabric a lovely visual balance.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Rainbow Dash's original Gala gown

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Fluttershy’s little garden of a Gala gown.

Fluttershy's first Gala gown was a rather tender study in botanical shapes. pale yellow-green and leaf-green panels overlapped and curled into a long soft rear drape. a broad pale-aqua band swept along the side, and white, yellow and aqua circles decorated the scalloped lower edge. a large cyan butterfly rested at the chest, and green vine-like straps curled above her shoes. the first fitting included a blue flower with a dark teal center in her mane; later styling included butterflies.

Rarity wanted the gown to reflect Fluttershy’s personality; to me, the garden-like shapes were a lovely expression of her affinity with nature. to my eye, the loveliest part was that the curves of the fabric themselves resembled growing leaves. the garden was present in the outline of the dress as well as in its ornaments.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Fluttershy's original Gala gown

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rarity’s own Grand Galloping Gala gown.

for the Grand Galloping Gala, Rarity’s finished gown had rich rose and fuchsia panels, deep wine-purple edges and sweeping golden-yellow bands across the layered skirt. its fitted front rose into a high collar and deep v-shaped opening with a bright jewel at the point. curved layers swelled over the hindquarters and fell into a long train. small oval or droplet-like accents sparkled on the fabric. a golden tiara with a pink-purple diamond-shaped centerpiece and smaller pink ornaments, earrings and jewelry framed her swept violet mane.

her friends helped finish her own design, with Fluttershy's sewing skill contributing to the result. she wore it to the Gala. i love that the great regal silhouette had a little history of friendship stitched into it.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Rarity's own Gala gown

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a study of restraint in Twilight Sparkle’s and Applejack’s revised Gala outfits.

when Twilight Sparkle and Applejack asked Rarity to revise their Grand Galloping Gala dresses, their requests led to two rather instructive experiments. Twilight's rejected version had a nearly black purple or navy skirt, yellow stars joined by actual constellation lines, a large yellow sun and white crescent moon, star-tipped projections over her head and a large turquoise tail bow with a star at its center. her wish for astronomical accuracy turned the night sky into something more like a chart.

Applejack asked for practicality. the resulting bright-blue overall-like garment was crowded with a brown-orange saddlebag, patches, multicolored rectangles and straps. she wore a green neckerchief, a tall red hat with white band and enormous green apple badge, and bulky yellow boots with dark soles. i wonder whether a dress can communicate a pony's virtues more gracefully by selecting a few details instead of illustrating every one.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Gala revisions · Twilight Sparkle and Applejack

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Pinkie Pie’s and Rainbow Dash’s rather exuberant Gala experiments.

when Rarity revised the Grand Galloping Gala dresses for Pinkie Pie and Rainbow Dash, Pinkie Pie's outfit became quite a party unto itself. great blue and aqua fan-like shapes projected outward beside yellow and vivid green sections. a huge green-and-yellow bow dominated the front, balloons of several colors hovered over the rump, and a giant cupcake with icing and cherry became her hat. yellow hoof accessories completed the look.

Rainbow Dash wanted extra coolness. her revision used bright red, sky blue and gold, a stiff-looking side panel with a white cloud and yellow lightning bolt, a tall flat rainbow-striped helmet crest with round golden sides, and angular golden hoof guards. what i notice in both experiments was the difference between suggesting an idea through the movement of cloth and collecting literal symbols of it. the designs made a wonderfully funny lesson in choosing a focal point.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Gala revisions · Pinkie Pie and Rainbow Dash

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Fluttershy’s rather extravagant garden-themed Gala redesign.

Fluttershy's rejected Gala gown was covered in garden imagery. a huge pale-green skirt carried pink-and-white flower circles and a scalloped green lower edge. a vast orange-red petal collar surrounded her upper body, leafy green coverings wrapped her hooves, and a bird's nest with blue eggs sat on her head.

what i find fascinating is that her original green Gala dress suggested nature through the curves of leaves, whereas this revision placed so many literal garden objects upon the wearer. a little restraint can give Fluttershy's gentleness more room to be seen.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Gala revisions · Fluttershy

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with the green and blue designs from Full Spectrum Fashions.

Sweetie Belle's arrangement of Rarity's materials inspired Full Spectrum Fashions. instead of putting every hue on a single dress, Rarity explored separate color families. the green mannequin wore a forest-green cylindrical top hat, a very dark hatband, three light-green round accents and a lime feather. a dark standing collar had three bright round buttons; sleeves ended in dark cuffs with lime dots. broad curved dark and medium-green skirt bands met lime stripes near the shoulders.

the blue mannequin wore oval blue headband beads, a rounded breastpiece in dark, medium and light-blue bands, a broad layered hoof cuff and a bead bracelet. i particularly like the different kinds of rhythm: curved bands and a tall feather in the green, rounded jewelry-like shapes in the blue. a single hue has rather more possibilities than one might suppose.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Full Spectrum Fashions · green and blue

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with the costume of Ponyville’s mysterious hero, Mare Do Well.

Rarity made the costumes for the mysterious Mare Do Well. each costume had a broad purple hat with a dark navy band and an irregular pointed crown, a fitted purple body covering and a navy full-face hood with two large pale-blue eye shapes. a midnight-blue cape swept behind the wearer. the purple collar rose in points at the shoulders, and a round pale-blue chest medallion carried a purple M. navy hoof boots had blue outlines and curved horizontal stripes like overlapping wraps.

Rarity’s friends took turns portraying one hero, with even a flying appearance by Fluttershy. what i find clever is how the covered face, repeated emblem and distinctive purple-and-blue silhouette made different ponies recognizable as the same mysterious character. that is an excellent exercise in designing a shared visual identity.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Mare Do Well

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Twilight Sparkle’s lovely little yellow birthday dress.

the birthday dress Twilight Sparkle received from Rarity was a lovely little exercise in restraint. soft lemon-yellow fabric hung in an almost tunic-like shape over her back, leaving the forelegs and tail free. a broad rounded pink neck edge tied into a generous bow at the chest, with two pointed ends. a narrow cream or white line finished the lower hem.

Rarity made the gift out of gratitude, and Twilight appreciated its simplicity. the bow was the focal point of the design. there was no need for a trailing skirt or a constellation of gems. sometimes the beautiful thing about a gift is that it has been chosen for the pony who receives it.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Twilight's yellow birthday dress

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a ruffled taffeta cape and the story of a fire ruby.

Rarity studied earlier fashions and anticipated the return of ruffled taffeta capes. Spike's gift of a fire ruby inspired her new line of taffeta capes. the one she wore was a bright pink drape with a dark magenta standing collar, pale pink curling ornaments at the neck and a light blue clasp. the cape was torn during the upheaval in Ponyville.

at Rarity's throat, the fire-ruby necklace had a conspicuous faceted, heart-shaped red stone with orange-red highlights, framed by a thick golden-colored rim on a smooth golden neck band. Spike had given her the gem, and i couldn't say who made the setting. i love how the restrained setting gave the ruby so much presence. a gift can become the beginning of an entire creative idea.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · ruffled taffeta and the fire ruby

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Cranky Doodle Donkey’s magnificent Dreamboat Special.

the Dreamboat Special! Pinkie Pie commissioned a replacement toupee from Rarity for Cranky Doodle Donkey. rather than his earlier dark wig, this one was golden blond, with a tall pompadour sweeping backward to a point. curved lock lines, a pale yellow highlight and short pointed locks behind the ears gave the shape definition. a little curved lock sat near the forehead.

what a delightful use of silhouette. the upward volume and backward sweep lent the whole profile a rather confident character. Rarity achieved that transformation without making a single dress. my lilac mane is particularly appreciative of a good curl.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · the Dreamboat Special

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a look at two royal bridal presentations.

before the royal wedding, Chrysalis, disguised as Princess Cadance, demanded more beads and a longer train. her visible gown had a broad white skirt, thick yellow-gold horizontal scrollwork, gold chest ornament and gold hoof shoes. a translucent veil fell from alternating turquoise-and-white flowers. i don’t know whether Rarity made two separate finished gowns.

Princess Cadance's own wedding look used white and cream, warm golden scroll-like shoulder and chest decoration, a turquoise accent near the neck and pointed or scalloped gold-colored shoes. her translucent veil began at a cluster of pale-yellow and cream rose-like blossoms at the base of her horn, leaving her pink, purple and cream mane visible. i particularly like how the different floral arrangements changed the way the two bridal looks framed the face.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · the two bridal presentations

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rarity’s flower-and-polka-dot bridesmaid dress.

at the royal wedding, Rarity wore a bright cyan drape with pale polka dots tapering into a pointed train. a pink dotted petal-shaped overlay sat above it. a mint-green ribbon at the neck held a pink diamond-shaped ornament. a light-aqua headband supported green rosette-like flowers with pink centers, and her forelegs were bare.

i particularly love how the repeated dots and flowers connected those two distinct areas of color. the pointed cyan train drew the eye backward, while the green floral headband brought the composition back toward her face.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Rarity's royal bridesmaid dress

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rarity’s signature curled textile for the Manehattan fashion competition.

before the Manehattan fashion competition, Rarity had spent months developing a plum or mauve textile covered in little pale spiral curls. it stretched without clinging and had a controlled shimmer, according to Rarity. she used it for her original collection.

what fascinates me is the way those tiny spirals suggested motion while the fabric's actual stretch allowed movement. the plum field gave the pale curls a lovely definition. a designer can give a whole collection a recognizable language through its fabric alone, even before deciding on the shape of each dress.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Manehattan's signature curled textile

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Hotel Chic, the collection that grew out of a hotel room.

with her Manehattan collection compromised, Rarity and her friends made a winning replacement from hotel-room textiles and furnishings. Hotel Chic took its inspiration from the hotel itself. the designs suggested sweeping drapery, enormous tie-back-like bows, decorative bands, tassel-like forms and distinctive hats.

among the Hotel Chic design sketches, a large pink-purple pony study wore a tall lavender hat, a huge green bow at the neck, a narrow vertical front ornament and a long teal scalloped train. the drawing recorded a design concept, rather than the finished runway gown. what i find enchanting is the way a room's rhythms can become the rhythms of a dress. even a piece of furnishing meant for an entirely different purpose can suggest an intriguing silhouette.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Hotel Chic · a room becomes a runway

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a pair of Hotel Chic studies in draping and banded fabric.

two Hotel Chic concept studies showed very different ways to handle fabric. on the light-aqua pony sketch, a small layered high-neck or shoulder piece met a short body band, followed by a long gray drape beneath the much paler shoulder fabric, gathered behind the haunches. a head detail swept upward. the aqua of the pony contrasted with the gray of the cloth. the long fall of fabric reminds me of curtains.

on a pale-mint model, a dark bow marked the neck, and a jacket-like short top met a compact rounded rear skirt divided by contrasting horizontal bands. the second composition felt more tailored and rhythmic to me. these were design sketches, so i don’t presume the eventual dresses had exactly these colors or materials. what a lovely study in the difference between a flowing surface and a structured volume.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Hotel Chic · long drape and banded skirt

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with two Hotel Chic sketches exploring the shape of a hat and a skirt.

in one Hotel Chic concept sketch, a violet pony wore a tall gray-purple hat flaring toward the top, with a white shirtfront-like chest area, a large contrasting bow and a dark ornament at the side. the flared hat reminds me of a lampshade, though that resemblance alone does not establish Rarity’s inspiration.

another sketch used a pale-yellow model, a short fitted upper section, a dark ribbon-like band and a large rounded skirt carrying pale circular or floral markings. there was a round detail near the mane. one placed its great statement high above the head, while the other spread the interest across the skirt. both demonstrated how the location of the visual focus changes the character of a silhouette.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Hotel Chic · tall hat and rounded skirt

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rarity’s rather extravagant country styling.

one rather extravagant rustic look featured an enormous pale-yellow woven-looking Western hat with ochre edging, curved straw-like marks and a wide hot-pink band made of lighter stripes. round cyan, magenta and purple ornaments clustered about the crown and brim. pale cloth at the chest and flank had bright-pink scalloped edges and scattered pink, purple and blue dots. i couldn't say who fashioned the hat itself.

i rather adore the contradiction: even when she tried to look rustic, her taste turned the hat into a spectacular focal point. the woven-looking surface was a lovely backdrop for all those little jewel-like circles.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Rarity's fancy country styling

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Over the Moon, a celestial gown from Royal Regalia.

for Over the Moon, Rarity took inspiration from Luna raising the moon. the fitted chest was nearly black indigo, with a purple high neck band, little white pearl-like circles, a white crescent and smaller four-pointed stars. dark rounded shoulder ornaments curled inward like spiral rosettes, edged in lavender scallops. a purple bow sat high behind the neckline, and little white dots traced the rear edge of the chestpiece.

the skirt rose over the back into long blue-violet layers with dark curved fold lines and scattered white dots and stars. irregular angular aqua and mint gem-like shapes formed a dense border at the hem. dark violet shoes repeated white crescents, turquoise dots and curling lines. oh, how my ears perk at the contrast between those dark curls and icy little accents. the placement of light upon that dark field is a delight.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Royal Regalia · Over the Moon

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with The Reign in Stain, also known as the Princess Dress.

The Reign in Stain, renamed the Princess Dress by Sassy Saddles, was inspired by the stained-glass window commemorating Twilight's coronation. a pointed deep-teal chestpiece formed a sharp v, with pale round ornaments in dark outlined cells. white feather-like pieces edged in icy aqua rose behind the shoulder; the forelegs remained bare. mint and aqua skirt panels flowed into brighter blue, then lavender and violet, ending in a long rear train. broad petal-like scallops defined the layers. dark curved lines divided the colored panels, with round green, blue and white jewel-like nodes at intersections and within the cells.

what fascinates me is how the window's organization became the organization of the garment, from the angular chest to the great curved panels and tiny round accents. the fabric suggested stained glass without having to be made of it. it was a particularly lovely example of transforming the structure of an inspiration.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Royal Regalia · The Reign in Stain, the Princess Dress

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a little mystery and tailoring inspired by Shadow Spade.

Rarity had already created her Femme Mystique Chic collection, inspired by the fictional detective Shadow Spade, before her own investigation in Canterlot. her detective jacket was muted brick-red or burgundy, close-fitting, with a standing collar, little dark button-like markings and gathered cuffs. a salmon-pink bow sat at the throat.

her investigation gave her a chance to show off the collection. i like how the fitted jacket and bow brought attention toward her face, a very different effect from the long sweeping trains of Royal Regalia. a beloved character from a mystery story can inspire a whole manner of presenting oneself without requiring every garment to have the same silhouette.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Femme Mystique Chic · Shadow Spade

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Masquerade, a rather understated Nightmare Night dress.

Rarity offered Fluttershy a look called Masquerade: a simple black dress with a narrow curved neckline, smooth fitted front, an opening for her wings and a long uninterrupted dark drape. it was paired with an ornate mask. Fluttershy chose the dress alone because the mask restricted her peripheral vision. the underlying gown remained the same.

to my eye, the simple dark fabric gave the accessory room to be spectacular, and the removal of the mask brought the focus back to Fluttershy herself. a single thoughtful adjustment changed both the appearance and the experience of wearing the costume.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Nightmare Night · Masquerade

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rarity’s shimmering mermare costume.

Rarity's mermare costume had a turquoise-to-blue fish-tail extension tapering behind her into a purple fin. pale green shell-like decorations, yellow-white dots and little scale marks ornamented the blue-green surface. her violet hair was swept into an elaborate updo with a pale mint shell-like accent and little white bead-like dots at the forehead.

the tail swung when she moved. the fin belonged to her costume rather than a magical transformation. i couldn’t say who made each piece. what delights me is the change in the outline of the pony. the aquatic shapes took the place of her usual faceted gems, while the long tail gave the silhouette another kind of movement.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Nightmare Night · Rarity's mermare

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Twilight Sparkle’s and Applejack’s contrasting Nightmare Night costumes.

Rarity's Nightmare Night group costumes included Twilight's ancient-warrior-like outfit: a bright gold helmet with cheek guards, a high curved red crest divided by narrow lines, and room for her horn. a gold breastplate with pointed shield-like center and curling ornament covered a deep blue-violet neck piece. overlapping pointed gold rear panels had little red dots and pale fabric beneath, with gold bands and shield-like leg guards.

Applejack's lion costume had a shaggy reddish-brown mane framing her face, roundish triangular ears, her own blond forelock showing, a smooth tan-brown body and shaggy cuffs above pale paw covers marked with little dark claws. i love the contrast between the warrior's carefully repeated angular shapes and the lion's expressive soft volume. the two costumes suggest rather different approaches to shaping the materials.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Nightmare Night · Twilight Sparkle and Applejack

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Pinkie Pie’s and Rainbow Dash’s playful Nightmare Night costumes.

Pinkie's Nightmare Night skating outfit featured two huge round hot-pink hair puffs, a pale-aqua visor, a short aqua top with bright blue-green edging, and a purple lower garment edged in white and mint. aqua-and-purple striped legwear met light-mint roller skates with dark purple wheels, bright cuffs and little purple bows. matching protective-looking cuffs continued the palette.

Rainbow Dash wore a transparent-looking round astronaut helmet with mint-green edging and a pale inner cap showing pointed ear shapes. her white and pale-mint suit had green outlines, two round chest discs, geometric harness lines, curved torso bands and pale boots with mint outlines and round mechanical-looking accents. wings and rainbow tail remained visible. to my eye, Pinkie’s look expressed athletic energy, while Dash’s evoked celestial exploration.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Nightmare Night · Pinkie Pie and Rainbow Dash

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Rarity’s rather striking punk reinvention.

Rarity's punk look replaced the familiar curls with long, pointed, sweeping locks of mint green, deep purple and bright yellow. her dark eggplant-purple sleeveless jacket was fitted, with a high sharp collar and an open front showing her white chest. pale blue-white round studs traced the collar and curved arm opening. a dark strap ended in a light rectangular silver-colored buckle, echoed by a dark studded hoof cuff. pale-blue eye shadow and dark lashes finished the look.

this was her response to a hair mishap. i admire the way she styled the jacket, whether or not she made it herself. my lilac curls are quite fond of her usual style, but i admire this transformation. repeated ornaments and carefully balanced color remained Rarity's language, even when she spoke it in points rather than spirals.

for the full catalogue, check the attachment provided
tracks.title: astra · art of the dress · Rarity's punk reinvention

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a little act of tailoring for Capper and his burgundy coat.

on her travels, Rarity repaired Capper's long burgundy or red-brown coat. it had a raised pointed collar, fitted long sleeves, dark cuffs, an open front and pointed lower tails. she stitched the torn seam at his sleeve cuff and added two round gold-colored buttons, one on each lapel, whose little bright circles stood out against the dark cloth. this was a garment made for an upright cat, not for a four-legged pony, and she was repairing it, not creating its original pattern.

what i find so lovely is the smallness of the intervention. she didn't need to replace the whole coat to bring out its character. two well-placed golden points can restore definition to the front of an existing garment. there is a kind of generosity in knowing which parts of a design ought to remain as they are.

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Yona’s finished Amity Ball ensemble.

Yona's finished Amity Ball dress was a strong green drape around her rounded shaggy body, with a darker green band, pale aqua accents and an enormous bright-blue flower at the side with a golden-yellow center. her horns and feet were still visible. the makeover included a massive swept purple wig with a magenta stripe, round pale-aqua earrings and blue-green cosmetic accents. the wig and grooming were as much a part of the ensemble as the dress itself.

the flower created a clear focal point against the green. yet the great change to her hair and silhouette makes me wonder what a design developed around Yona’s own preference for brown and her yak identity might have looked like. helping someone feel at home in a beautiful outfit is a different undertaking from making them resemble a familiar pony silhouette.

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Twilight Sparkle’s celestial coronation gown.

Twilight's final coronation gown had a lavender or periwinkle front, crossed by a folded icy-blue diagonal sash. at the breast, a golden-yellow star-shaped ornament held a vivid magenta starburst. a white or pale-lavender gathered band curved across the back behind her wing. the long lavender skirt carried three visible pale many-pointed stars near the wing, darker purple overlapping curved folds toward the rear, and a thick light-blue train border. pale ice-white hoof coverings rose into pointed crown-like tops. Twilight wore her striped mane in a raised ponytail for the ceremony.

Rarity had completed a coronation gown weeks in advance, though she still planned a last-minute sash of luminous star-spider silk. i particularly like the way the celestial theme of Twilight's first Gala dress matured into a single strong emblem and a few carefully placed stars. it was a distinct royal commission, not the retail Princess Dress.

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with Twilight Sparkle’s separate backup coronation gown.

Rarity fitted a separate backup gown for Twilight’s coronation. it used desaturated slate-blue and teal with pale-aqua and icy-blue accents. a fitted front had small rounded scallops along its lower edge. several broad rounded skirt panels hung vertically to the rear, shaded deeper blue toward the top. a pale blue-white drape crossed the back and dropped in a long vertical side panel.

what i particularly appreciate in the backup is its tonal character: the pale drape set against the darker skirt, the quiet rounded contours, and a different visual emphasis from the star-decorated primary gown. Rarity's preparation gave us another distinct study in royal dress, even though this particular fitting did not establish that Twilight wore the backup to the ceremony.

tracks.announcement_text:
and now we take in the art of the dress, with a reflection on beauty and individuality in Rarity’s designs.

i find a beautiful distinction between an exquisite object and an exquisite relationship between an object and its wearer. for the Grand Galloping Gala, Rarity gave Twilight Sparkle stars on blue fabric, while Applejack’s warm brown and green gown had golden fringe and an apple clasp. the Princess Dress turned stained-glass tracery into dark curves across mint, blue and lavender skirt panels. when Rarity repaired Capper’s burgundy coat, a few round golden buttons brought definition back to an existing garment.

the design questions were rather different in each case, yet what enchants me is the attention to the creature who would live in the design. i think a gown may be at its loveliest when its wearer feels more like herself, rather than like somepony else.

tracks.announcement_text:
There is rain at my window, friend. Little beads of water are collecting on the glass, and every so often two of them meet and make their way down together. I had meant to close my notebook some time ago. Instead, I have been watching the rain.

An empty page is a rather inviting thing. I thought I might fill this one with observations from a journey. Not a catalogue of all the places in existence, of course. I should be here with the notebook open for an extraordinarily long time if I attempted that.

There is an old forest I would like to visit. I have been thinking about its light, and about the way a familiar place becomes almost unrecognizable when one approaches it from another time. We shall begin there and see what other places suggest themselves along the way.

I shall leave the lamp beside this window. It is a small, ordinary light, and I am rather fond of it. Before we depart, I would like to remember the sound of this rain. There will be many other sounds on our journey, but this particular one belongs to the beginning.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 01 · a window at home

tracks.announcement_text:
The rain at my window has given way to a little wind among the leaves. I have come to the forest I had in mind. There is daylight here, though very little of it reaches the ground without first passing through something green.

The canopy makes a lovely arrangement of the light. A leaf moves, and a patch of brightness appears on a trunk. Another leaf moves, and that patch disappears. All along the forest floor these little alterations are happening at once. I could spend a considerable portion of the afternoon studying nothing but their intersections.

Ah, there is a particularly fine leaf caught in my lilac mane. I shall return it to the forest. It has quite enough to do here without accompanying me across spacetime.

My notebook is open again. I would like to compare this woodland with a much earlier moment in its history, before the little clearing beside me came to be. I have a good place from which to make that comparison. For now I shall remain among these trees and take a rather more careful look at their shapes.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 02 · the first change

tracks.announcement_text:
The clearing is gone. I have chosen an earlier part of the forest's history, and in the space that was open to the sky stands the trunk of a tremendous old tree. Its branches extend well beyond the patch of ground where I was standing before.

There is a curious pleasure in finding the same hillside in two different arrangements. The slope is recognizable, and a little outcrop of stone has much the same shape, yet the living things occupy the space differently. I have drawn the stone at the edge of both pages of my notebook. It makes a rather useful point of comparison.

Between the trunks I can hear water. I had noticed the valley on the way here, but was sufficiently interested in the leaves that I had not yet gone down to it. The wind is softer at this depth of the woodland. The sound of water becomes more distinct as the ground descends.

I think I shall follow the river out of the trees. There is another aspect of this landscape that I would like to see, and it will be rather pleasant to let the water suggest the direction of our next visit.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 03 · before the clearing

tracks.announcement_text:
Here is the river we heard among the trees. At the bend, the current pulls away from a bank of pale stones and forms a series of small, shifting eddies. The forest is still behind me, but its leaves have become the quieter sound of the two.

I have been watching a little fleck of light on the water. It seems to run across the surface and vanish whenever the angle changes. My first sketch of it has become a sketch of the entire bend. There are limits, even for a cosmic unicorn, to the usefulness of trying to draw a moving reflection.

Farther downstream the valley opens. I would like to visit the place where this water meets the sea, though not necessarily in the same morning that is unfolding here. I have chosen a dawn for that visit. The water will be part of the same landscape, at a very different instant in its travels.

Before leaving, I shall add the direction of the current to my page. A little arrow is sufficient. The river has been a rather good guide, and I need not draw every ripple to remember where it led.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 04 · where the river bends

tracks.announcement_text:
The river has reached the sea, and we have arrived at the dawn I selected. Its mouth lies behind a long, low bank of sand. There is a thin gold line on the horizon, while the water near the shore is still the color of the night.

The waves have a much broader rhythm than the running water at the bend. One comes forward, another overtakes it, and the sand briefly becomes a mirror. There is a delightful moment when the sky appears to lie beneath the surface of the earth.

Beyond the shore is a place I have been intending to revisit. In a different age of this coast, a city was built with chambers looking out into the sea. I should like to see its glass galleries again. We shall go by a different route than the waves, as there is no need to subject my notebook to a thorough soaking.

I can see the sun now. I shall leave the beach while the first light is still spreading across it. The next page will have rather more blue on it than this one.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 05 · the shore of another morning

tracks.announcement_text:
We are in the dry gallery of the city beneath the sea. The water is on the other side of a great curved window, and the light that reaches it passes through layers of blue and green before it reaches the floor.

The builders have made their arches echo the shapes outside. A broad window follows the outline of a shell, and another curves like a wave that has been held perfectly still. It is an elegant bit of architecture. I am particularly interested in a row of little marks where the glass meets the stone. They correspond to the tides. Someone has been observing the water here for a very long time.

There is an archive farther along this gallery. I have a particular weakness for archives, friend, especially ones whose shelves contain the observations of many different ages. I was going to make one drawing of the window. I now have three, and a small sketch of the tide marks besides.

The sea remains on the other side of the glass. I shall continue into the archive before I become sufficiently absorbed in the architecture to forget how many pages I have allotted to it.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 06 · a city of glass and tide

tracks.announcement_text:
The sound of water is very faint in this part of the city. The archive lies behind several thick walls, and its passages are lined with shelves that turn into little alcoves. There are drawings of fish, books about the changing shore, and a rather splendid collection of records of the sky.

One map caught my attention. It shows the coast as it was when the city's outer chambers were built. Beside it is another map from much later, and the two have quite different outlines. I have placed them side by side. The differences tell a story that neither picture tells on its own.

Between those records is an illustration of a kingdom inland, with bells drawn in the towers. I know the place. I had considered visiting it later in the journey, but the illustration has reminded me of a particularly beautiful view from its high terrace at evening.

I shall copy the little design of the bell into my notebook. Then we can visit the terrace in its own time, and hear something that this paper cannot quite preserve.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 07 · the library beside the sea

tracks.announcement_text:
There are the bells. We have come to the terrace above the kingdom whose towers I saw in the archive beside the sea. The evening light is making the stone look warmer than it is, and the little windows below us are beginning to shine.

A bell sounds from one tower and is answered, a moment later, from another. Their notes are different. I find the space between those notes particularly lovely, for the city has a sound of its own in the interval. A little wind moves across the terrace, and somewhere below, the garden paths are passing into shadow.

I have drawn the two towers in the margin next to the bell from the archive. It is gratifying to put a real sound alongside a picture I had been studying.

There is a garden on the lower side of this terrace. By midnight the lamps there will be much more distinct, and the bells will have become quiet. I think I shall visit that part of the kingdom then. I would like to hear what remains when the evening's more elaborate sounds have passed.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 08 · an evening in a distant kingdom

tracks.announcement_text:
The bells have finished. It is midnight in the garden below the terrace, and there is a much smaller music here, made by the little creatures among the leaves. There are patches of moonlight between the paths. The garden has not grown entirely quiet merely because the city has.

A few drops of water remain on the leaves from an earlier watering. I have been watching one of them catch the light of a lamp. It reminds me of the rain at my own window. How lovely that a very small reflection should recall a place so far removed from this one.

I had not intended to stay quite so long over a single drop of water. I have, however, made a rather pleasing little drawing of it. The lamp and the drop fit in the same corner of the page.

There is a winter landscape I would like to compare with this garden. The paths there will be covered in snow, and the little sounds of the night will be quite different. I shall leave this garden beneath its moon, with its lamps still glowing and its insects carrying on their quiet business.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 09 · the garden after midnight

tracks.announcement_text:
The garden's little nocturnal music has become a gentle winter hush. I have chosen a sheltered window overlooking a snow-covered valley. The flakes are small, and the outlines of the trees gradually become less distinct as the snow gathers on their branches.

The lamp beside this window belongs to the shelter, not the one I left at home. I rather enjoy the resemblance. The light falls across the sill in much the same way, though outside it is snow instead of rain that passes through the brightness.

There is a fine opportunity here to observe how an environment changes without anything having to move very far. A dark branch becomes white. The edge of a path disappears. A few pale shapes become the entire foreground of the view. My pencil is proving a rather inadequate instrument for drawing something almost entirely composed of variations in white.

Across the valley are the mouths of several caverns. I have selected one with particularly interesting reflections of sound. When I leave this window, I shall go there and listen to the valley from beneath its surface.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 10 · snow beyond the window

tracks.announcement_text:
The snowy window is behind us. I have come into one of the caverns across the valley. The rock overhead forms a series of curved surfaces, and a little water is making its way from one ledge to another.

A single drop makes several faint sounds in succession. The first comes from the ledge, and the others are reflections returning from different parts of the cavern. I have chosen a quiet place to speak so that my words need not compete with all those lovely little echoes.

There is a particularly graceful chamber near the entrance. Its arch reminded me of the underwater city's galleries, though here no one had to design the arch. I made a drawing of each on facing pages. It is interesting how often very different histories produce forms that invite comparison.

I have been thinking of a third arch: the roof of a transport platform in a distant future. I know a moment when it stands almost empty. It seems a fitting place to continue this little study of spaces and the sounds they hold. I shall leave the cavern to its water.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 11 · the valley of echoes

tracks.announcement_text:
We have reached the platform I had in mind. Its canopy is a delicate arch, and at this particular hour there are no passengers waiting beneath it. The faint sound from farther along the structure belongs to machinery at rest between journeys.

Above the edge of the platform is a sign whose lights change very slowly. The architecture is extraordinarily practical. Every curve that appears decorative also seems to have been chosen for a purpose. I had intended to draw the roof alone, but the arrangement of the lights deserves a page of its own.

The city beyond the platform is still here. I have simply selected a quiet interval in its day, rather than arriving in the middle of everyone's travels. I am rather fond of seeing a place when the things designed to serve its inhabitants have a little time to themselves.

From this finished structure, I would like to visit a landscape that has not yet acquired anything resembling a city. There is a world still taking shape in its own peculiar way. The comparison may make for a rather interesting pair of pages.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 12 · tomorrow's empty platform

tracks.announcement_text:
There are no platforms or lamps here. I have reached the world I wanted to see while its landscape is still forming. Pale ridges rise against a dark sky, and farther away the ground glimmers with colors that shift as the surfaces change.

This is a rather different kind of construction from the one we saw in the future city. There is no builder's plan on a wall, no sign indicating where the next road will lie. I am content to observe the extraordinary arrangement before me without assigning it a purpose it may not possess.

My silver sigil catches the light of the nearest ridge. Ah, that is a beautiful little reflection. I shall make a note of its color, though I suspect the color will be rather difficult to reproduce on paper.

Above the landscape are several lights I recognize. I would like to leave the ground behind for a time and consider the sky from another vantage. I have selected a quiet view of the stars, where I can attend to those lights without the shifting colors of the landscape continually enticing me back to my drawing.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 13 · a world still being made

tracks.announcement_text:
We have left the forming landscape, and the stars occupy almost the whole of my view. There is a particular pair I have been looking forward to seeing. One shines with a warmer color than the other, and their positions make a lovely little figure against the surrounding darkness.

Light has its own history, even when the object emitting it seems motionless from where we look. In the ordinary physical universe, we see distant objects through light that has spent time reaching us. I find that thought especially pleasing when I have a quiet view such as this one.

There is only the faintest glimmer around my horn. I have kept this part of our visit especially quiet; the view deserves a little room of its own.

I have made a sketch of the two lights. Beside it I shall leave a considerable amount of empty paper. There is a place between my visits where I sometimes like to contemplate what I have seen. We shall spend a little time there, without another landscape insisting upon being drawn.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 14 · a light from long ago

tracks.announcement_text:
The stars are no longer in view. I have chosen a quiet interval between destinations, and for a little while there is very little around my voice. No forest, no water, no bells. The page beside the drawing of the stars remains mostly empty.

I have been turning back through the notebook. The little arrow on the river page. The map from the underwater archive. The towers and the midnight lamp. I notice that I have drawn rather more lamps than I had anticipated when I sat beside my window at the beginning.

I think it is useful to leave some room between observations. Otherwise I am liable to become so interested in the next discovery that the previous one receives scarcely a moment of contemplation. And there is a great deal here that I should like to remember accurately.

I have not quite finished the journey. There is a particular region of spacetime where I would like to examine a faint signal. It has a rhythm that interests me, and I shall turn my attention to it when we leave this little interval. For now, the silence is a very agreeable companion.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 15 · the quiet between worlds

tracks.announcement_text:
I have reached the region where I intended to examine that faint signal. It has a recurring pattern, two little intervals close together, followed by a longer one. I have been examining its pattern rather than amplifying the signal over our broadcast.

It reminds me of the rain at home. Not because the signal is rain, or because I have concluded that it comes from my window. The resemblance is one of rhythm, and that is quite enough to set a curious mind comparing things.

I had begun a calculation on this page, and somehow the corner has acquired another little drawing of a lamp. Mmm. I shall put the calculation in the middle, where it may have rather more space.

The rhythm has also reminded me of an orchard I know, whose trees look quite different in successive seasons. I would like to see those changes together as a study. We need not follow this signal to a mysterious destination. I have heard enough of it for the observation I wanted to make, and the orchard is calling to my curiosity now.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 16 · a familiar rhythm, elsewhere

tracks.announcement_text:
Here is the orchard. I have selected a succession of moments from the same place. First, the branches are nearly bare. Then there are pale blossoms, summer leaves, and finally a beautiful gathering of autumn colors.

I shall not try to describe every change at once. The trunk of the tree beside me provides a useful constant, rather like the outcrop of stone I drew in the forest. I can compare the spread of its branches in each season and give the changing leaves a place in the same drawing.

There is a breeze through the orchard. It seems quite different when there are blossoms on the branches from when the branches are bare. I find that delightful. Even the sound of a place depends upon what the living things are doing there.

At the edge of the orchard stands a shelter with a very familiar arrangement of windows. I would like to examine it in the autumn moment, when the light is particularly fine. I shall remain in that season for our next visit. The other drawings can keep their own dates.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 17 · the orchard of seasons

tracks.announcement_text:
We are inside the shelter at the edge of the autumn orchard. The leaves are still golden outside the window. There is a small lamp on the sill and a surface on which I can rest my notebook. The whole arrangement looks rather like the one I left at home.

It is not my room. The window has a different shape, and the light falls from the opposite side. Beyond the glass is the orchard, rather than the particular view I remember. I am pleased by the likeness, but the differences are quite as interesting.

I have drawn this window alongside the snowy one and the little lamp from the garden. Apparently I have been making a study of windows as well as a study of changing landscapes. How curious. I had not set out with that particular subject in mind.

There are a few places I would still like to visit before returning to my own window. I have chosen a route that will bring me back through the rain and the distant kingdom, though not quite in the order of our outward journey. I shall close the notebook for the passage between them.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 18 · a room that almost feels like home

tracks.announcement_text:
The orchard shelter is behind us. I have begun the return portion of my journey, and the surrounding light has a rather lovely folded appearance. I have chosen the next few visits deliberately. It is pleasant to travel with room for curiosity, and equally pleasant to decide that one has had quite enough pages for a single excursion.

My notebook contains a series of little drawings that were not part of my original intention. Windows, lamps, reflections, a drop of water. The places were very different, yet those small things kept catching my attention. I need not turn the resemblance into a great mystery. It has made a rather lovely pattern in the notebook all by itself.

We shall visit a rain-covered hillside before returning to the kingdom with the bells. I have a reason for choosing that hillside. There is a view through its rain that I would like to place beside the first page of the journey.

The light around us is growing softer now. I shall keep the broadcast quiet as we make the passage.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 19 · the path that returns

tracks.announcement_text:
The soft light of the passage has given way to rain on a hillside. We are not home yet. I have chosen a little covered place from which to watch the rain crossing the open landscape.

At home I was watching beads on a pane of glass. Here I can see the rain passing over several distant ridges. The nearest one is quite distinct. Farther away, the outlines become pale and almost dissolve into the sky. It is a lovely example of depth made visible by the atmosphere.

My mane has acquired the tiniest collection of droplets along its curls. I had leaned a little too far beyond the shelter to see the nearest ridge. The notebook, I am pleased to report, has remained quite dry.

The rain belongs to this hillside, just as the rain at the beginning belonged to my window. I shall draw the two views on facing pages. Then we can leave the hillside and return to the kingdom at dawn. The towers we heard at evening will have a rather different appearance when the light comes from the other direction.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 20 · rain on the hillside

tracks.announcement_text:
We have left the rain on the hillside and returned to the terrace above the kingdom. It is dawn this time. The windows that shone in the evening are much less conspicuous, and the towers have taken on a pale color in the morning light.

Ah, there is the bell I remember. I can distinguish the two notes now, and I have added their relationship to the little drawing from the archive. A picture of a tower is quite a different thing when one has also heard its bell.

Below the terrace is the garden we visited at midnight. It lies in the same place, but the shadows have been replaced by the growing light. I shall leave the garden as it is. There is no need to revisit every corner simply because it has become possible to do so.

Before returning home, I would like one last quiet view of the stars. I have chosen a vantage beyond this morning's bright sky, where I can place the last little celestial drawing in my notebook. Then I shall go back to my window and the lamp I left there.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 21 · a kingdom at dawn

tracks.announcement_text:
The kingdom's morning has fallen behind us. There is one particularly lovely star in the view I have chosen, with a little companion point of light nearby. I shall give them the remaining space on the page beside the earlier drawing of the stars.

I have enjoyed taking you along, friend. The journey has become a rather different collection of observations than I imagined while watching the rain. I had expected to fill most of the notebook with extraordinary landscapes. There are several of those, certainly. But there are also some rather ordinary things, which have proved quite as worthy of a place.

I am going to return to the window from which I began. I know the moment I have chosen: the lamp is still glowing, and the rain has not yet passed. It will be pleasant to hear that familiar sound again after so many changes of surroundings.

I shall leave the stars to their own histories. There is a little space at the bottom of this page, but I think I know what belongs there. I will fill it in when we arrive.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 22 · one last star

tracks.announcement_text:
There is the rain. We are home, friend. The lamp beside the window is just as I left it, and a few drops have gathered along the lower edge of the glass. I have returned to the moment I had in mind.

I can put my notebook on the familiar surface again. The drawing of the snowy window is open, and beside it is the drawing from the orchard shelter. It is rather amusing to compare them with the actual window in front of me. They share a few lines, but none has quite this arrangement of light.

The rain on the hillside is recorded near the end of the notebook. The rain at home is on the very first page. I have drawn the small lamp in the space that remained beside the last star, as I intended to do. It is a pleasing conclusion to the little collection of lights.

I shall remain here for a while. The journey is over, but there is one page I would like to look through before I put the notebook away. The rain can keep us company until I have finished.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 23 · the familiar window

tracks.announcement_text:
The rain continues at my window. I have been looking through the notebook one last time. The old forest, the river, the city beneath the sea, the archive, the bells, the winter valley and the little intervals between the stars. It is a rather full notebook for something that began with a single empty page.

What I particularly like is that each place remains distinct. I need not decide which of the windows was the finest, or which of the lights was the most extraordinary. They belong to different moments of the same journey, and I am glad to have attended to each in its turn.

The silver sigil on my flank glimmers with quiet affection. My lilac mane has finally settled into a rather more orderly arrangement, and the lamp is making a warm little circle on the surface beside me.

I shall close the notebook now. There is no particular hurry to open another. For a while, I would simply like to listen to the rain. And when another journey begins, this will still be a rather lovely place from which to set out.

It is good to be home, friend.
tracks.title: anywhere, anywhen · 24 · home, again

tracks.announcement_text:
There is a little trap in the familiar names of trees. Douglas-fir is not a true fir, and western redcedar is not a true cedar. They are all conifers, but their names do not place them in the same genera.

A genus is a group of related organisms. In the scientific name of a species, the first word identifies its genus; the second helps distinguish the species within that genus. True firs belong to a genus called Abies. Douglas-fir belongs to Pseudotsuga. Western redcedar belongs to Thuja, whereas true cedars belong to Cedrus.

Common names are useful for conversation, and I have no wish to discard them. But when two books use different common names, a scientific name helps establish whether they are discussing the same organism. A rather elegant little system, especially when one considers how much variety there is in the trees alone.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: the names of trees

tracks.announcement_text:
Suppose you wish to identify an unfamiliar tree. I would begin with its leaves, not with its height. Does it have broad leaves, needles, or tiny overlapping scales? If it has needles, are they attached separately or gathered into bundles? If it has broad leaves, do two leaves emerge opposite each other, or does each occupy its own position along the twig?

These are examples of the questions used in a dichotomous key. At each step there are two descriptions, and you choose the one that agrees with the specimen. A good key leads you toward a smaller and smaller set of possibilities.

The cones, fruit, buds, bark, and geographical range can help confirm your conclusion. One particularly misleading leaf is rather less troublesome when several other features agree. I would keep a regional key close to hoof and learn the distinctions a little at a time.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: a key without a lock

tracks.announcement_text:
A Douglas-fir has a rather splendid identifying feature in its cones. Between the rounded scales are projecting bracts with three points. The middle point is long, with a shorter point on either side. Imagine little pitchforks tucked between the scales of a hanging cone.

The needles are attached individually, relatively flat, and the buds are often quite pointed. That is already a useful distinction from a pine, whose needles commonly grow in bundles. A true fir, on the other hoof, usually bears its seed cones upright, and those cones break apart as they mature.

A Douglas-fir cone may fall to the ground largely intact. A true fir cone is less likely to present itself to you in that convenient form. Look for the three-pointed bracts first. If you encounter them on a woody hanging cone, you have one of the most delightful clues in the conifer collection.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: Douglas-fir

tracks.announcement_text:
I rather like the foliage of western hemlock. Its needles are short, and the needles along a single twig are often noticeably different in length. They tend to form a flattened arrangement, with pale markings underneath. The leading shoot at the top of the tree frequently droops.

Its seed cones are small, oval, and hang down. Compare one with the larger Douglas-fir cone, which bears those distinctive three-pointed bracts. The western hemlock's cone is a much tidier little affair, without the conspicuous projecting pitchfork shapes.

A drooping treetop alone would not be sufficient evidence for a firm identification. But if the top droops, the little needles differ in length, and the small hanging cones agree, you have several clues working together. Western hemlock is an important tree of the moist forests of the Pacific Northwest. Do not confuse this conifer with the unrelated plants commonly called poison hemlock.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: western hemlock

tracks.announcement_text:
The western redcedar offers a useful departure from the individual needles of firs and hemlocks. Its foliage is composed of tiny, overlapping scales, arranged in flattened sprays. A little branchlet looks almost as though its leaves have been woven together.

The bark of a mature tree is often reddish brown and fibrous, with long vertical strips. Its small woody seed cones have a handful of scales, rather than the elaborate form of a large pine cone. Those features belong to a tree in the cypress family, despite the word cedar in its common name.

There are other conifers with scale-like foliage, so the flattened sprays are a beginning, not the entire identification. Compare the pattern of branching, the cones and the bark. In the coastal forests of the Pacific Northwest, a combination of flattened sprays and long fibrous bark is a particularly worthwhile clue to remember.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: western redcedar

tracks.announcement_text:
Among the coastal conifers, Sitka spruce has needles that can be quite sharply pointed. Each needle is attached to a small woody projection on the twig. When the needles are lost, those projections can leave the twig feeling rather rough.

Compare that with a true fir twig, which is generally much smoother where the needles have detached. The cones of Sitka spruce hang down, and their thin scales have irregular, somewhat jagged edges. These provide better evidence than trying to recognize a spruce from its outline at a distance.

Sitka spruce is strongly associated with the moist coastal region of western North America. Habitat can help narrow an identification, though trees are sometimes planted well beyond their native range. I would remember the sharp needles, the little woody pegs, and the delicate edges of the cone scales. A most useful combination of three features.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: Sitka spruce

tracks.announcement_text:
A grand fir often has a particularly neat arrangement of needles. On many of its shaded twigs, longer and shorter needles project to the sides, producing a rather flattened spray. The needles are glossy above and have pale bands beneath.

A true fir's seed cones stand upright on the branches. When mature, they usually disintegrate there, leaving their central axes. You may search the ground beneath a fir for an intact seed cone and find that the tree has been quite uncooperative in that respect.

Compare this arrangement with Douglas-fir, whose hanging cones may retain their scales and projecting bracts after they fall. Both trees can have flat individual needles, so the way the needles are arranged and the form of the cones are important. Grand fir occurs in the forests of the Pacific Northwest; use a regional key to distinguish it from its fellow true firs.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: grand fir

tracks.announcement_text:
Noble fir and grand fir are both true firs, yet the foliage of a typical noble fir has quite a different appearance. Its needles often curve upward, and their pale bands can give the branches a lovely bluish or silvery cast. Grand fir's shaded branchlets more often have a flattened arrangement of needles extending to the sides.

The seed cones of noble fir are large and upright. The bracts project beyond the scales, giving a mature cone a rather elaborate surface. Like other true fir cones, these generally break apart on the tree.

A tree can change the appearance of its foliage depending on the age of the branch and how much light it receives. I would therefore compare several branchlets rather than trust a single needle. Look also at cone characters and the habitat. The difference between these two firs is a delightful example of how closely related trees need not look quite alike.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: noble fir

tracks.announcement_text:
Western hemlock and mountain hemlock are members of the same genus, but they are not the same species. The western hemlock often has short, unequal needles arranged in a rather flat plane. Mountain hemlock tends to carry its needles around the twig more evenly, giving the foliage a fuller, sometimes bluish appearance.

The cones of mountain hemlock are generally longer than the little oval cones of western hemlock. Its natural habitat often lies higher in the mountains, where the winters bring considerable snow. Western hemlock is especially familiar in moist forests at lower elevations, although the ranges of these trees can overlap.

I find the needle arrangement a useful starting point. Flat-looking sprays or needles reaching in several directions? Follow that observation with a look at the cones and a check against the regional key. A difference in elevation is helpful, but not an identification in itself.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: two hemlocks

tracks.announcement_text:
Here is a delightful little exercise in identifying pines. Find a natural bundle of needles where it attaches to the twig. Count the needles that emerge from that single base, rather than counting all the needles gathered around the branch.

Many familiar pines have two, three or five needles in a bundle. Western white pine commonly has five. Ponderosa pine typically has three, although the count can vary. Lodgepole and shore pine generally have two. A pine's bundle, or fascicle, is a useful distinction from the single needles of Douglas-fir and true firs.

The number does not identify every pine in the world. Several species may share a count, and some are rather less predictable. The length and stiffness of the needles, the shape of the cones, and the tree's range all contribute further evidence. But it is an excellent first question to ask of an unfamiliar pine.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: counting pine needles

tracks.announcement_text:
Shore pine and lodgepole pine can look remarkably different in their usual surroundings. A shore pine growing near the coast may have a low, irregular form shaped by its exposure. Inland lodgepole pines often grow tall and narrow. Yet these names refer to varieties of the same species, Pinus contorta. The coastal variety and the inland varieties differ in inherited characteristics as well as in the conditions under which they grow.

The needles are usually paired, relatively short, and often a little twisted. The cones and the tree's surroundings supply additional information. The name lodgepole refers to the tall, comparatively straight trunks that the inland form can produce.

This makes an interesting distinction between identifying a species and describing the shape of an individual tree. A coastal wind can alter the form of a tree without creating a new species. If you have found a pine with two needles per bundle, friend, do not stop there. Compare its cones, needle lengths, and habitat with a reliable local key.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: shore pine and lodgepole pine

tracks.announcement_text:
Ponderosa pine has long needles that are typically gathered in bundles of three. The needles may form conspicuous tufts toward the ends of branches. Mature trees often have thick bark divided into broad plates, which can take on an orange or yellowish-brown color.

Its seed cones are woody and have prickles on the ends of the scales. The combination of long needle bundles, cone characters, and the plated bark provides considerably better evidence than bark color alone. Young ponderosa pines, after all, may look quite different from their much older neighbors.

The species is associated with many comparatively dry forests in western North America. Compare it with the two-needle lodgepole pine or the five-needle western white pine. Counting at the base of a bundle can save a surprising amount of uncertainty. I find the older bark rather beautiful, too, with its irregular little islands of warm color.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: ponderosa pine

tracks.announcement_text:
Five slender needles in a natural bundle are a characteristic feature of western white pine. Its needles tend to be comparatively soft, and its long, narrow seed cones hang from the branches. The cone scales are rather different from the thick, prickly scales familiar on some other pines.

Several pines share the five-needle arrangement, so I would not assign a species name on that evidence alone. In western North America, whitebark pine and other five-needle relatives are also worth considering. The cone, its manner of opening, and the habitat can help distinguish them.

The count is useful because it brings you to a smaller collection of possibilities. Then the long, slender cones of western white pine provide another clue. Once you begin to notice the difference between needles growing singly and needles growing in bundles, conifers become a considerably less mysterious collection of trees.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: western white pine

tracks.announcement_text:
Is a conifer necessarily evergreen? Western larch provides a rather beautiful answer. It bears cones and has needles, but in autumn its needles turn golden and fall. Through winter its branches can be almost entirely bare, before new needles emerge in spring.

On the older short shoots, the needles grow in conspicuous clusters. On the elongated new shoots, they may be distributed singly. This arrangement is different from the little bundles with fixed counts found in pines.

The words conifer and evergreen describe different characteristics. A conifer belongs to a particular lineage of seed plants, whereas evergreen describes the retention of foliage across seasons. Western larch demonstrates why the two words are not interchangeable. On a mountain slope, a larch can contribute a lovely patch of gold to a landscape that otherwise remains predominantly green. It has not ceased to be a conifer merely because the season has changed.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: the deciduous conifer

tracks.announcement_text:
Bigleaf maple bears leaves that can be wonderfully large, with five principal lobes spreading like the fingers of an open hand. Vine maple also has a palmate leaf, but its leaves are generally smaller and typically have more lobes, usually seven, though the number can range from five to nine.

Both trees have opposite leaves and produce paired winged fruits called samaras. Those paired fruits, together with the opposite arrangement of leaves or buds, help distinguish a maple from several unrelated trees with lobed leaves.

A bigleaf maple can grow into a substantial forest tree, while vine maple frequently forms a smaller, spreading or many-stemmed plant. But the shape of a plant is influenced by its conditions, so the leaves and fruits make a useful comparison. Bigleaf maple's name is rather obliging in this respect. A particularly enormous leaf with five main lobes is a lovely place to begin looking.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: bigleaf maple and vine maple

tracks.announcement_text:
Red alder has a useful feature along the margins of its leaves. The leaves are toothed, and the edges often roll slightly underneath. The leaves are arranged alternately along the twig, rather than in the opposite pairs found on a maple.

You may also notice little woody, cone-like structures remaining on the branches. They are the persistent structures from the female catkins. Although their appearance is reminiscent of little conifer cones, an alder is a flowering plant, not a conifer.

Red alder can grow rapidly on disturbed sites and is familiar in moist Pacific Northwest landscapes. Its roots may participate in a partnership with nitrogen-fixing bacteria, an interesting subject quite apart from the tree's appearance.

For identification, remember the toothed leaves with rolled-under edges and the small woody structures on the branches. The presence of something shaped like a cone is not, by itself, sufficient to establish that a tree is a conifer.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: red alder

tracks.announcement_text:
Pacific madrone is particularly recognizable when one sees its bark. The reddish or orange outer layers peel away, often revealing a smooth greenish surface beneath. The tree also has broad, rather leathery leaves that remain on the plant through the winter.

A broadleaf tree need not be deciduous. The madrone is an evergreen flowering tree, quite unlike the evergreen conifers with needles or scale-like leaves. Its flowers and berries provide additional clues when they are present.

The twisting form of older madrones and the changing colors of their bark can be quite beautiful. I would still examine the leaves and other identifying characteristics rather than rely entirely on a reddish trunk, since other trees can have peeling bark.

This is a pleasing counterpart to the larch: one is a conifer that sheds its needles in autumn, and the other is a broadleaf flowering tree that retains foliage throughout the year.
tracks.title: astra's observatory: Pacific madrone

tracks.announcement_text:
Three broadleaf trees provide a useful comparison. Oregon white oak commonly has leaves with rounded lobes and produces acorns. An acorn, especially when its cup is present, is an excellent clue to the genus of oaks.

Paper birch is familiar for its pale bark, which may peel in thin layers. Look also for the little horizontal markings known as lenticels, and examine the toothed leaves. Bark color alone can be deceptive, particularly on young trees.
